'''Mustafar''' was a young, small [[planet]] located in the [[Mustafar system]], within the [[Atravis sector]] of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Once a [[Plant|garden]] world nourished by the [[Bright Star]] artifact, its [[orbit]] was shifted when [[Lady]] [[Corvax]] [[Aeon Engine|unleashed]] the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to [[Immortality|return]] her [[Dorwin Corvax|husband]] to life. The resulting [[Gravity|gravimetric]] duel between the [[gas giant]]s [[Jestefad]] and [[Lefrani]] over Mustafar [[Temperature|heated]] the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced [[Volcano|volcanic]] [[Chaos|hellscape]]. Adapting to life on their devastated [[homeworld]], the [[arthropod]]al [[Mustafarian]]s evolved into [[Northern Mustafarian|two]] [[Southern Mustafarian|distinct]] [[Species|subspecies]] that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Corvax's search for immortality brought the ancient [[Sith]] to Mustafar, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a [[Sith temple (Mustafar)|temple]] over a [[Vergence|locus]] in the [[dark side of the Force]], above the buried ruins of [[Corvax Fortress]].

Acquired by the [[Techno Union]] over three hundred [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Clone Wars]], Mustafar's [[Magma|lava]] flows were [[Mining|mined]] for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the [[Black Sun]] crime syndicate, whose [[Black Sun fortress|headquarters]] was located near the mining [[City|town]] that became known as [[Zitontown]] after the [[Falleen]] [[Ziton Moj]] [[Mission to Mustafar (Death Watch)|ascended]] to leadership of the organization. As part of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the Clone Wars, the Techno Union on Mustafar [[Techno Union droid factory|produced]] [[battle droid]]s for the [[Separatist Droid Army]]. [[Darth Sidious]] had a [[Darth Sidious's secret facility|secret facility]] on the planet where he intended to turn "[[Project Harvester|harvested]]" [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|children]] into [[The Force|Force]]-talented [[Spy|spies]]. However, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] had the base scuttled when [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] and his [[Padawan]], [[Ahsoka Tano]], arrived to [[Mission to Mustafar (Skywalker and Tano)|rescue]] [[Wee Dunn|the]] [[Zinn Toa|younglings]].

Mustafar served as the [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility|final redoubt]] of the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] until the newly-appointed [[Darth]] Vader, formerly Anakin Skywalker, was [[Mission to Mustafar|sent]] by Sidious to [[Death|slaughter]] the council, effectively ending the Clone Wars. The [[Sith Lord]] was confronted by his [[Marriage|wife]], [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], and his former [[Jedi Master]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. The latter [[Duel on Mustafar|dueled]] Vader, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Vader was saved when Sidious arrived and carried him offworld. Mustafar then came under the ownership of the [[Galactic Empire]] after the Techno Union and its assets were nationalized. Sidious had new facilities built on the planet, where more Force-sensitive infants were taken and transformed into agents of the [[Inquisitorius]].

During this [[Imperial Era|era]], Vader returned to the site of his greatest defeat and, with the help of the ancient Sith Lord [[Darth Momin]], [[Battle of Fortress Vader|erected]] the massive monolith [[Fortress Vader]] to serve as his personal sanctum, built on the [[Sith cave|site]] of the former [[Sith temple]]. Throughout the Age of the Empire, Vader used the planet to fulfill his master's biddings, with the fiery world becoming the final resting place for [[Jedi|victims]] of the [[Great Jedi Purge]]. In addition, Vader also undertook personal business within his new realm, attempting to wield the dark powers of Mustafar to bring his deceased wife back from the dead.

Following the Dark Lord of the Sith, the Empire took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Mustafar were taken over by the [[Mining Guild]], although strict Imperial travel restrictions on the [[Star system|system]] made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Black Sun also abandoned Mustafar for a more low profile world when the Empire established a [[Fortress Vader Imperial garrison|garrison]] there. The Mustafarians resisted the Imperial occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Mustafar by launching [[Raid on Fortress Vader|multiple]] [[Attack on Fortress Vader|assaults]] on Fortress Vader.

Although it hosted one of the [[Action at Mustafar|earliest rebel victories]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]], Mustafar fell into obscurity following Vader's demise at the [[Battle of Endor]], though Black Sun did eventually return to the planet. After the [[Battle on Mustafar|destruction]] of the Bright Star, the planet's ecosystem slowly began to heal from the devastation it had endured for [[Standard century|centuries]] prior. Many devout pilgrims journeyed to the ruins of Fortress Vader, hoping to tap into the late Sith's dark power. [[Standard decade|Decades]] after Vader's death, his grandson, [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]], [[Mission to Mustafar (First Order)|journeyed]] to the world to continue the legacy of his [[Skywalker family|family's]] grisly past. The [[Supreme Leader]] of the [[First Order]] slaughtered the [[Alazmec of Winsit|Sith cult]] that defended Fortress Vader and discovered his grandfather's [[Vader's wayfinder|Sith wayfinder]], a tool that allowed him to locate the phantom [[Galactic Emperor|emperor]] Sidious on [[Exegol]].

==Description==
===World of fire===
{{Quote|Mustafar is a lava planet, terrible place, full of awful mines. There's a custom there to jump lava flows and…well, you'll see.|L3-37|<ref name="Lando's Luck">''[[Lando's Luck]]''</ref>}}
Mustafar was a young<ref name="BMF 17" /> rocky [[planet]] within the [[Mustafar system|eponymous system]]<ref name="ROTS" /> of the [[Atravis sector]], in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. It was a small world<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> situated in grid square L-19<ref name="TFABG" /> of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]],<ref name="Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> and it lay on the [[Tosste Spur]] [[Hyperspace route|trade route]], off the [[Rimma Trade Route]].<ref name="BMF 17" /> A part of the [[Western Reaches]],<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Mustafar was located 53,000 [[light-year]]s from [[the galaxy]]'s [[Core Worlds|Core]].<ref name="BMF 17" />

[[File:MustafarSurface-MF85.png|thumb|left|350px|The landscape of Mustafar was harsh and filled with lava.]]
With an overlapping [[orbit]],<ref name="FF" /> Mustafar was the third orbit of its [[Star system|system]] around the primary [[star]] [[Priate]],<ref name="BMF 17" /> completing a [[Local day|full rotation]] every 36 [[standard hour]]s<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> and a revolution around its sun every 412 local days, the equivalent of 618 [[standard day]]s.<ref name="year note" /> It had a diameter of 4,200 [[kilometer]]s,<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> or 2,610 miles,<ref name="VE" /> and was a terrestrial world classed as a wasteland during the Imperial Era.<ref name="BMF 17" />

Nourished by the power of the [[Bright Star]] artifact, it was once a<ref name="Immortal 1" /> temperate and<ref name="BMF 33" /> [[Plant|lush]] garden world that thrived with lifeforms that inhabited [[forest]]s.<ref name="Immortal 1" /> [[Millennium|Millennia]] before the Imperial Era, Mustafar [[Devastation of Mustafar|became]] an unstable [[Volcano|volcanic]] world with underground [[cave]]s<ref name="BMF 17" /> and free-flowing<ref name="BMF 42">{{BuildFalconCite|42|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> [[Magma|lava]] constituting 35% of its<ref name="BMF 17" /> volatile<ref name="BMF 42" /> surface,<ref name="BMF 17" /> taking the form of lava [[Ocean|seas]],<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> rivers,<ref name="CL" /> and pits<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> interspersed with glens, molten rock plains,<ref name="TROS VD" /> as well as [[obsidian]] [[mountain]] ranges<ref name="CL" /> and shores.<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Few areas were temperate enough to sustain life, and only a few landmasses were not fractured by tectonic disruption and magma flows; allowing lifeforms to evolve deep underground.<ref name="BMF 33" />

The tortured planet<ref name="BMF 17" /> was powerful in the [[dark side of the Force]],<ref name="DV5">[[Darth Vader (2017) 5|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 5]]</ref> and, along with valuable [[mineral]] allotropes that surfaced from the planet core<ref name="CVD" /> as well as its obscurity to the wider galaxy, attracted various off-world interests that exploited the molten planet.<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> Mustafar remained a [[Fire|fiery]] world until the destruction of the Bright Star, at which point the planet was allowed to regrow.<ref name="Immortal 3">{{VaderImmortal|III}}</ref> Such different states of the world led some to believe that spiritual forces were the catalysts to the changes in Mustafar's nature.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Despite the planet's rugged and dangerous nature, there was a deadly beauty to the volcanic landscapes.<ref name="BMF 85">{{BuildFalconCite|85|Secrets of Spaceflight}}</ref>

===Heart of lava===
{{Quote|Of all the fumes that drift up from the lava lakes deep underground, these were the most potent. They played tricks with your head…making you see things that weren't there. Shadows of the mind. Fears… doubts… ghosts of the past.|Lellis, on Mustafar's lava fumes|<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />}}
Deep underground, Mustafar contained lava lakes from which [[Lava fume|fumes]] drifted up to surface-level facilities; such [[Gas|fumes]] played tricks with the minds of organics who inhaled it, giving rise to what [[Lellis]] referred to as "shadows of the mind"—visions of fears and doubts that could manifest as ghosts of the past. Lava fumes were most potent around the vicinity of the [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility]], and sustained exposure to it drove an individual insane. [[Repulsor vent]]s were thus installed at the Mining Complex to prevent such toxic fumes from rising to indoor facilities and being inhaled by those within.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

[[File:Jestefad.png|thumb|right|360px|Mustafar and its twin, Jestefad]]
Mustafar was twinned with the [[gas giant]] [[Jestefad]], which it closely orbited, being constantly pulled by its [[Gravity|gravitational]] force; Mustafar was nearly captured by the larger world as its [[moon]], an event that was only prevented by the counterbalancing gravitational pull from the more remote gas giant [[Lefrani]]. Mustafar nevertheless possessed a standard gravity. The influence of the massive magnetic field of Mustafar's larger twin, however, resulted in its [[Chaos|hellish]] volcanic landscape, as the power of Jestefad's gravitational force caused massive tidal disruption that heated Mustafar's interior.<ref name="CL" />

Along with being engulfed in a constant gravimetric battle, Mustafar housed an unstable core that caused [[groundquake]]s powerful enough to split the planet's continents apart,<ref name="TROS JN">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]''</ref> and its split tectonic plates allowed the planet's searing magma to push through to the surface, creating a volcanic hot spot visible as a bright red cluster from [[Realspace|space]].<ref name="TROS VD" /> Most stable areas of land were prone to erosion from the lava or abrupt reshaping due to the earthquakes.<ref name="BMF 85" />

While great portions of the planet were always in motion, one of the few constant features was the [[central volcano]]. Lava poured out of the spot at nearly 100,000 [[liter]]s per [[second]] and pooled at the giant volcano's base. To the north was a region named the [[Burning Plains]], which boasted heavy volcanic activity. Another region earned its nickname, the [[Smoking Forest]], as smoke spewed from its [[tree]]-like rock chimneys. Mustafar's [[Berken's Flow]] was the largest lavafall in the galaxy, while [[Tulrus Island]]<ref name="BMF 17" />—which shared its name with the [[tulrus]] creature<ref name="BMF 33" />—was surrounded by tall mountains.<ref name="BMF 17" />

[[File:MustafarBackdrop-SWH.png|thumb|left|250px|Mustafar featured rivers of lava.]]
The young<ref name="BMF 17" /> world's instability churned magma that carried [[ore]]s<ref name="TROS VD" /> with unique and valuable minerals<ref name="Calendar2020">[[Star Wars Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2020|''Star Wars'' Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2020]]</ref> to its surface,<ref name="TROS VD" /> attracting business interests<ref name="CL" /> from various<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> galactic [[mining]] conglomerates<ref name="TROS VD" /> such as the [[Mining Guild]]<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> to exploit the mineral wealth of the otherwise untouched world.<ref name="CL" /> Mining facilities were set up for minerals and metal ore,<ref name="AEYNK" /> including [[dolovite]],<ref name="SW11" /> [[gold]],<ref name="CL" /> [[mirkanite]],<ref name="BMF 17" /> and [[bronzium]].<ref name="Prospect Paintwork" />

The searing magma that bubbled beneath the surface flooded the planet, covering it in oceans<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> and rivers of lava. Geothermal energy was the main power source of the [[Techno Union]]'s mining complex on the planet,<ref name="CL" /> and the lava flows that coated the rocky terrain left behind traces of [[flood basalt]].<ref name="DV21">[[Darth Vader (2017) 21|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 21]]</ref> At 800°C (1500[[°F]]), Mustafar's lava, while still very hot, had a lower [[temperature]] than that found on other worlds due to unusual mineral allotropes that were molten at lower temperatures.<ref name="CL" /> Nevertheless, patches of Mustafar began to cool in the [[Standard decade|decades]] leading up to<ref name="TROS VD" /> [[35 ABY]].<ref name="Timelines" />

===Tempestuous skies===
[[File:FDKF_FC_BG_art.png|thumb|right|300px|The electromagnetic interference in Mustafar's atmosphere posed a risk to travelers.]]
Mustafar's atmosphere was influenced by the breath of its volcanoes and Jestefad's massive magnetic field. Along with cyclonic-force updrafts and thermal currents, titanic lightning storms made up the planet's unfriendly skies. Turbulent and ash-laden,<ref name="CL" /> the atmosphere was also hot and chemical,<ref name="TROS EE" /> consisting of thick clouds of black smoke<ref name="Dark Disciple" /> and allowing for<ref name="TROS JN" /> choking ash<ref name="AEYNK" /> to fall like rain.<ref name="TROS JN" /> Lava processing operations created toxic gas by-products,<ref name="CL" /> and a noxious air cast the world in a hazy fog.<ref name="TROS EE" /> Thus, Mustafar was classified as a world with a Type II atmosphere, wherein the usage of a [[breath mask]] was recommended.<ref name="BMF 17" />

The frequent<ref name="CVD" /> electromagnetic interference and lightning storms in the atmosphere respectively led to signal loss and noise, although the effects of Mustafar's hectic skies could be reduced through the use of dedicated dampers.<ref name="CL" /> The planet's magnetic field interfered with [[sensor]]s installed on the surface,<ref name="CR 4">[[Crimson Reign 4|''Crimson Reign'' 4]]</ref> and electromagnetic interference also posed a significant risk for off-world arrivals and departures.<ref name="CL" /> Those caught in one such storm<ref name="DV21" /> without the assistance of specially shielded surface-level landing equipment<ref name="CL" />—which included energy-shielded<ref name="CVD" /> landing pads and [[Guide beam|guidance]] and [[tractor beam]]s—found, at best, their [[starship]]'s scanners rendered useless and navigational equipment and control systems interfered with.<ref name="CL" /> In certain cases, a ship was torn apart<ref name="DV21" /> as Mustafar was by Lefrani and Jestefad.<ref name="CL" /> Ships were additionally threatened by Mustafar's intense heat and incendiary ash, although any damage could be prevented should a vessel be equipped with sufficiently powerful [[Deflector shield generator|energy shields]].<ref name="CV">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref>

===Fauna and flora===
====Hardy beasts====
=====Lethal predators=====
[[File:Darkghast-art.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The cavernous underground of Mustafar was home to ferocious creatures (darkghast pictured).]]
Despite the hellish environment after its devastation, Mustafar was teeming with life, a home to fragile but determined organisms all connected through [[the Force]] energy field.<ref name="TROS EE" /> All surviving lifeforms had evolved deep underground, in the few areas that remained temperate and with landmasses were not fractured:<ref name="BMF 33" /> in the solid rock betwixt lava flows lived [[mammal]]ian, [[Reptile|reptilian]], and [[insect]] [[species]],<ref name="BMF 17" /> although reptilian and [[insectoid]] lifeforms proved to be the most successful survivors, aggressive in nature and with tough skin or carapaces.<ref name="BMF 33" /> The extremophile creatures of the planet had adapted to Mustafar's desolation and become indomitable.<ref name="TROS EE" /> The [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Mustafarian]]s were insectoid,<ref name="AEYNTK UE" /> and were forced to live largely underground in Mustafar's north and near the equator.<ref name="SM" />

Much like the planet itself, some of the creatures found on Mustafar were especially deadly.<ref name="Immortal 2" /> Highly aggressive creatures posed a significant hazard on the planet due to its scarce resources.<ref name="SM" /> The planet's apex predator was the [[scorpion]]-like [[Sher Kar]], which lived deep in the nesting grounds of their tulrus prey.<ref name="BMF 33" /> The fearsome [[darkghast]], similar in some respects<ref name="Immortal 2" /> to the [[rancor]]s of the planet [[Dathomir]],<ref name="CE UE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> was a multi-[[limb]]ed [[Diet|carnivore]] that dwelled beneath the world's rocky surface.<ref name="Immortal 2" />

The reptilian [[blistmok]] hunted in packs and were capable of pursuing their prey for days.<ref name="BMF 33" /> The insectoid [[xandank]]s were well protected by their armor and<ref name="GA">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> hunted in packs as well.<ref name="BMF 33" /> Tough, semi-sentient creatures<ref name="HC33">{{HelmetCollectionCite|33|Databank A-Z}}</ref> named [[roggwart]]s hunted the planet's tunnels and lava tubes in search of xandanks,<ref name="Cyborgs">{{BuildR2Cite|53|Droid Directory}}</ref> as well as for giant, [[human]]-eating<ref name="SW11">[[Star Wars (2015) 11|''Star Wars'' (2015) 11]]</ref> [[lava eel]]s. Despite the danger of roggwarts, they could be domesticated with the proper training<ref name="Cyborgs" /> and were imported to Mustafar to work in the planet's mines.<ref name="AEYNTK UE" />

By [[3 BBY]], a roggwart named [[Kongo]] the Disembowler was employed to keep the [[Dolovite mines of Mustafar|dolovite mine]] tunnels free<ref name="GA" /> of xandanks and lava eels.<ref name="SW11" /> Kongo was reputedly the last of his kind<ref name="HC33" /> by [[0 ABY]],<ref name="Star Wars 11 date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the [[rescue of Luke Skywalker]] to [[0 ABY]]. As [[Kongo]] was said to be the last of his [[Roggwart|kind]] during the rescue of [[Luke Skywalker]], it can additionally be determined that he was reputed to be the last of his kind by 0 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]].</ref> although it may have been said in an effort to make the roggwart seem more mysterious and exotic.<ref name="HC33" />

=====Creatures with other diets=====
{{Quote|The very ''beasts themselves'' conspire to thwart my vision. Fascinating. Utterly fascinating.|Lord Momin, reacting to a lava flea attack on Fortress Vader|<ref name="DV23" />}}
[[File:Lava-fleas-walking.png|thumb|right|320px|Northern Mustafarians ride lava fleas along a molten river.]]
The large insectoids known as [[lava flea]]s had developed a tough exoskeleton that protected them from the world's fiery devastation.<ref name="AEYNK" /> They lived largely underground<ref name="BMF 33" /> and ate away at the planet's crust,<ref name="AEYNK" /> feeding on the surface's rich minerals, rocks, and dirt and were commonly used as domesticated mounts by the sentient Mustafarians. Lava fleas and Mustafarians thus had a close connection and were the only species that thrived on Mustafar.<ref name="BMF 33" />

The large, lumbering egg-laying tulrus had sharp tusks and bad temper, while the small [[jundak]] parasite attached itself to a host and eventually burst out, killing the host and developing into a large adult.<ref name="BMF 33" /> [[Lizard-crow]]s occupied Mustafar's lava fields; these creatures were often scared away by what the Mustafarians referred to as "[[Molten man|molten men]]."<ref name="Return 5" /> [[Spark-roach]]es<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> and [[rodent]]s called [[fire rat]]s also called Mustafar their home, the latter of which gnawed on the [[lava crystal]]s that formed on the planet.<ref name="Return 1" /> A [[Unidentified Mustafarian ant|species of thick-skinned ant]] native to the world was known for its painful bite, which left behind burning pustules not unlike the volcanos that painted the planet's surface.<ref name="Beware the Nameless">''[[The High Republic: Beware the Nameless]]''</ref>

[[Lava nymph]]s were winged creatures that inhabited the planet's caverns in hives. Considered to be vermin, the creatures' insides were filled with lava, which they were able to spit out when provoked.<ref name="Immortal 2" /> Feeding on minerals, hives of [[kubaza beetle]]s lived near lava flows and were fierce defenders of their nests;<ref name="BMF 33" /> starting life as a small [[larva]], the creature developed a defense mechanism by the time it reached adulthood that allowed it to warn its brood by exploding.<ref name="Tales 2">[[Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle 2|''Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle'' 2]]</ref> Burrowing quadrupeds known as [[krishel]]s inhabited Mustafar's labyrinthine caverns and tunnels. Those strong, hard-shelled creatures were hunted by the Mustafarians.<ref name="SM" />

====Plants and fungi====
[[File:Corvax-Fen-TROS-VD.png|thumb|left|320px|Irontrees were some of the few plants found on the world.]]
Although the lush vegetation that once covered the planet eventually disappeared beneath fire and ash,<ref name="Immortal 1" /> Mustafar was not devoid of [[Fungus|fungal]] and [[Vegetable|vegetal]] life. Hidden away from the world's searing lava rivers, [[Kahel cave fungus|kahel cave fungi]] grew underground. These organisms were deeply symbolic to the native Mustafarians and served as the inspiration for their [[mushroom]]-like architecture.<ref name="CL" /> Following the destruction of the [[Aeon Engine]] during the Imperial Era,<ref name="Inside Intel">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-mustafar|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: Mustafar|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}}</ref> the muggy [[Swamp|marshland]] of<ref name="TROS JN" /> [[Corvax Fen]] developed near Fortress Vader,<ref name="Inside Intel" /> and life began to slowly creep back once again.<ref name="Immortal 3" /> By 35 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> barren [[irontree]]s stood in the few places where fertile soil existed, including the fen.<ref name="TROS VD" />

==History==
===Cataclysm immortalized===
{{Quote|Once, our world Mustafar was green, filled with life.|The Priestess teaches Mustafar's past to the descendant of Lady Corvax|<ref name="Immortal 1" />}}
[[File:CorvaxsDeath.png|thumb|right|300px|A battle (pictured) on the forest world of Mustafar claimed the life of Lord Corvax, prompting Lady Corvax to steal the Bright Star.]]
In its ancient past,<ref name="TROS VD" /> Mustafar was a lush and [[forest]]ed<ref name="Immortal 1" /> terrestrial planet,<ref name="BMF 17" /> thriving with life through the Bright Star, the native Mustafarians' most sacred artifact that nourished<ref name="Immortal 1" /> the small<ref name="CL" /> garden world.<ref name="TROS VD" /> It housed an [[Jedi enclave (Mustafar)|enclave]] of the [[Jedi]],<ref name="BMF 33" /> servants of the Force,<ref name="TROS VD" /> that drew attention from the Jedi's enemy, the [[Sith]]. After a thousand [[Standard year|years]] of skirmishes between the two groups, they came to a titanic battle in the Mustafar system that brought havoc to Jestefad, Lefrani, and Mustafar five thousand years before the Imperial Era.<ref name="BMF 33" />

Ancient legends said that offworlders led by [[Lady]] [[Corvax]] and her [[Dorwin Corvax|husband]] arrived at some point, living in harmony with the natives, but the garden world was [[Attack on Mustafar|attacked]] and Corvax's husband fell in battle against the invaders. Unable to let go of her love, Corvax stole the Mustafarians' Bright Star in her pursuit of [[immortality]], having thought it had the power to resurrect her husband from [[death]]. Corvax created the Aeon Engine and encased the artifact within, although her actions ultimately resulted in the devastation of the planet;<ref name="Immortal 1" /> energies ruptured from the Bright Star, pushing Mustafar out of its original orbit.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Other legends claimed that due to a cataclysmic struggle between the Sith and the Jedi, the orbit of<ref name="BMF 17" /> the gas giant Lefrani was also shifted, and Mustafar entered an unusual and gravitationally crushing alignment between<ref name="SM" /> it and Jestefad's magnetic fields.<ref name="BMF 17" />

With the [[devastation of Mustafar]], the world's new, precarious orbit rendered it a volcanic wasteland<ref name="Immortal 1" /> as both gas giants pulled on tiny Mustafar, heating its interior in their attempts to claim Mustafar as their moon.<ref name="CL" /> The crust of the smaller world was also torn apart, allowing the flow of lava toward the planet surface.<ref name="BMF 17" /> Very few species survived the cataclysm,<ref name="SM" /> with the homes of nearly all native species being destroyed. The remaining life-forms evolved<ref name="BMF 17" /> deep underground, in the few areas temperate and stable enough to support life,<ref name="BMF 33" /> and developed short, tough bodies to endure the superheated clime,<ref name="BMF 17" /> and the Mustafarians were forced to areas in Mustafar's north and near the equator. There, they adapted and evolved to the new realities of life on Mustafar.<ref name="SM" />

These events passed into legend, attracting Sith who were looking for the secrets of eternal life. Eventually, a [[Sith cave|Sith shrine]] was built<ref name="TROS VD" /> on the world's [[Gahenn Plains]]<ref name="DV23" /> as part of a [[Sith temple (Mustafar)|Sith temple]],<ref name="USWNE">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref> at the site of Lady Corvax's underground [[Corvax Fortress|castle]].<ref name="Immortal 1" /> The Jedi had been forced to abandone their enclave on Mustafar following its devastation, and the world was used by a Force organization named the [[Blackguard (Mustafar)|Blackguard]]. At some point, a Jedi and another individual fought a Sher Kar on Mustafar.<ref name="BMF 33" />

===A colony for mines and an outlaws' cove (c. 300–22 BBY)===
[[File:Mustafar_DB.png|thumb|left|266px|Mustafar's surface transformed into a hellish landscape.]]
Over three hundred years before the [[Clone Wars]], the Techno Union came to own the planet<ref name="CVD" /> due to its mining interests. Mustafar was a typical mining world of a Republic Era that was dominated by large-scale commerce and industry—volcanic, profitable, and dangerous. Although volcanic worlds like Mustafar were convenient for mining due to the naturally occurring furnace, but the savings could quickly be eaten up elsewhere.<ref name="BMF 85" /> The Techno Union built giant mining stations<ref name="BMF 33" /> at key locations<ref name="BMF 85" /> across Mustafar, where much of the ore extraction was done through heavily automated electromagnetic processes, and they led to valuable elements congealing as scum on top of the lava.<ref name="BMF 33" /> Many of such facilities were located at deep, fast-flowing lava rivers, as they could be scanned for passing ores or tapped by multi-prong collector arms. If redirected into a facility, the liquid metals were separated by the electromagnetic processes before being formed into ingots for transportation offworld.<ref name="BMF 85" /> The corporation provided the Mustafarians with tools to mine mineral allotropes for them,<ref name="CVD" /> labor which served to pay the rent that the Union charged.<ref name="TROS VD" />

[[Colonist|Mixed]] with workers of a great variety of other species, Mustafarian miners lived in simple residences at dedicated<ref name="TROS VD" /> rough-and-ready<ref name="BMF 85" /> mining towns, many of which were run-down. In addition to this,<ref name="TROS VD" /> the lack of water on the planet posed issues particularly for miners coming from offworld. Despite many of the miners being local, a fair amount came from other places in the galaxy and did not have the hardened nature to deal with the intense heat. The lack of water on the planet thus posed several issues, particularly for offworlders. Although water shortages were common, it did not stop the miners from brewing their own [[Alcohol|hooch]] that was popular among the locals.<ref name="BMF 85" /> Miners rode lava fleas<ref name="Dark Disciple" /><ref name="CL" /> or were helped by Techno Union technology for transportation.<ref name="SM" />

While Mustafar was similar to other mining planets in some ways, it also had unique qualities. Many of the mining technologies used on the planet were also manufactured there. Smart smugglers and independent spacers knew this fact. Part of the wealth of mining was shared by such individuals, who could make credits transporting workers or resources. Many of Mustafar's mining companies also used their own shipping companies. Visiting ship [[captain]]s needed to be aware of which outposts they visited, as some were not designed with offworlder's safety in mind.<ref name="BMF 85" />

While bigger installations manned by offworlders required extensive plant shielding, other, smaller ones rarely had these protections, as local Mustafarians often made use of individual lava flea armor instead. Modern mining facilities required plant shields, as even the strongest alloys and protective gear would not last long without them. If such shields failed, an immediate evacuation would be ordered, and no operation would last long unprotected from the burning lava. Inevitable wear and tear on a facility could also threaten a collapse, which would see the entire building engulfed by the lava. On the occasion of a volcanic eruption damaging a town, residents would likely be stranded if their ships were harmed, with no choice but to work as miners to earn enough to leave Mustafar.<ref name="BMF 85" />

The Trade Union supplied Mustafarians with technology such as the [[Baktoid Armor Workshop|Baktoid]] [[UH-XH Heavy Work Platform|UH-XH]] [[repulsorlift]]-powered platforms,<ref name="SM" /> lava-processing centrifuges,<ref name="CL" /> [[electrorefining droid]]s,<ref name="VE" /> and the [[DLC-13 mining droid]]<ref name="AEYNK" /> to collect mineral-rich lava spewing from Mustafar's heated interior,<ref name="CL" /> with the [[ore extraction droid]] also seeing use.<ref name="ROTS" /> Minerals were transported across the galaxy to words such as [[Nal Hutta]], where a shipment infested with Mustafarian ants found its way into the hands of [[Churo]] the [[Hutt]]<ref name="Beware the Nameless" /> in [[228 BBY]].<ref name="Beware the Nameless Date">{{StarlightDate|''[[The High Republic: Temptation of the Force]]''|one [[Standard year|year]] and six weeks after the destruction of Starlight Beacon|[[228 BBY]]}} Since ''[[The High Republic: Beware the Nameless]]'' takes place one year and six [[Standard month|months]] after the destruction of Starlight Beacon, its events must be set in 228 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] as well.</ref> Over the [[Standard century|centuries]], Mustafarians became wary of technology that<ref name="CVD" /> failed under the intense heat of their world and which had an inadequate melting point, having been witness to mechanical breakdowns. Such was the case for [[speeder]]s, including the heavy-duty UH-XH, which were generally left to be operated by [[droid]]s.<ref name="SM" /> Nevertheless, by the Clone Wars' end, Mustafar had served as a literal gold mine for the Techno Union for almost three hundred standard years.<ref name="CL" />

[[Damask Holdings]] also established a presence on Mustafar through a base.<ref name="BMF 17" /> In addition to its mining activities, desperate offworlders and law-evaders who were undeterred by the world's harsh conditions were drawn to Mustafar as a result of the obscure world's sparse population.<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> Mustafar was also ideal for hiding or disposing items in secret.<ref name="BMF 17" /> On the world [[Felucia]], an [[Unidentified individual (Qui-Gon Jinn)|individual]] romantically involved with the Jedi Padawan [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] in [[60 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines" /> gifted him a rare [[Mustafar fire diamond]].<ref name="M&A">''[[Master & Apprentice]]''</ref> In [[40 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> [[Gemstone|jewel]] [[Thief|thieves]] [[Pax Maripher]] and [[Rahara Wick]] discussed whether they should collect Mustafar fire diamonds, with Wick dreading the notion of doing so, before deciding to travel to the planet [[Pijal]] for [[kyber crystal]]s instead.<ref name="M&A" />

===Revenge of the Sith (22–19 BBY)===
====Scum and villainy====
=====Schemes in the shadows=====
{{Quote|I sense something, Master. And I don't like it.''"<br />"''It's the dark side, Ahsoka. This is the right place.|Ahsoka Tano and Anakin Skywalker|audio=TheDarkSide-CotF.flac|<ref name="Children of the Force">{{TCW|Children of the Force}}</ref>}}
[[File:BlackSunLeaders-Eminence.png|thumb|right|320px|Mustafar was a haven for crime, home to the leadership of Black Sun (pictured).]]
During the Clone Wars, the Mustafarians aligned themselves with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. However, they were not fanatically committed to the cause, having only joined to secure themselves Separatist contracts, and life continued much as it had before. With members of the [[Jedi Order]], the [[galaxy]]'s guardians of peace and justice, focused on defeating the Separatists, [[Law enforcement agency|law enforcement]] found itself in a declining state, especially in the infrequently patrolled Outer Rim. Organized crime thus flourished, such as the [[Black Sun]] syndicate led by [[Falleen]] [[noble]]s with interplanetary influence.<ref name="SM" />

The Falleen operated clandestinely,<ref name="BS DB">{{Databank|black-sun|Black Sun}}</ref> establishing elusive holdings on Mustafar<ref name="SM" /> and headquartering themselves in a well-defended [[Black Sun fortress|fortress]],<ref name="BS DB" /> where they regularly met<ref name="SM" /> and found the surrounding lava useful for the disposal of evidence.<ref name="Dark Disciple" /> The native Mustafarians cared little for Black Sun, since most of their operations took place elsewhere in the galaxy.<ref name="SM" /> Hidden away from prying eyes, the Techno Union also [[Techno Union droid factory|produced]] [[battle droid]]s behind their Mustafarian mining operations, situated within the same mountain as their Klegger Corp Mining Facility, at the time of the Clone Wars. By the time of the war, Darth Sidious was familiar with the existence of the Sith temple<ref name="CL" /> at the Gahenn Plains.<ref name="USWNE" />

[[File:SidiousMustafarLab-CotF.png|thumb|left|300px|Darth Sidious maintained a secret facility on Mustafar that was intended to train kidnapped Force-sensitive children.]]
Aside from skirmishes and lesser operations, fighting largely passed Mustafar by during the Clone Wars,<ref name="SM" /> resulting in the planet retaining a reputation as a remote astronomical object that individuals usually only stopped on to [[Fuel|refuel]]. Nevertheless, the planet bore witness to a [[Mission to Black Stall Station|plot]] to kidnap [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|children]] by [[bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane]], who was under the employ of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Sidious]]. Traveling on his [[Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighter|starfighter]], the ''[[Xanadu Blood]]'', Bane deposited the children at Sidious' secret [[Darth Sidious's secret facility|facility]], where the [[Sith]] planned to create an army of [[Spy|spies]] strong in the Force. The two children, the [[Gungan]] [[Roo-Roo Page]] and the [[Rodian]] [[Wee Dunn]], were to be prepared for a surgical procedure meant to enhance them, as Sidious aimed at having an army of Sith spies to counteract the Jedi. Upon reading through the captured ''Xanadu Blood''{{'s}} fuel logs, Jedi Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]] reasoned the world could be where Bane deposited the kidnapped children so she and her [[Teacher|mentor]], [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], traveled to Mustafar to [[Mission to Mustafar (Skywalker and Tano)|rescue]] the children. As the Jedi arrived at the facility, Darth Sidious ordered the [[RO-series childcare and nanny droid|nanny droids]] to destroy the installation so as to ensure the loss of any evidence of the plot. The [[nanny droid]]s attempted to relocate the children, but Skywalker and Tano managed to rescue them as the facility sank into the lava lake below it.<ref name="Children of the Force" />

In [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> renegade Sith Lord [[Maul]], his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]] [[Savage Opress]], and [[Pre Vizsla]], the leader of the [[Mandalorian]] [[terrorist]] organization [[Death Watch]], [[Mission to Mustafar (Death Watch)|traveled]] to the Black Sun fortress with the intention of recruiting them to their newly founded criminal empire, the [[Shadow Collective]].<ref name="Eminence" /> As four [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport|''Kom'rk''-class fighter/transports]] landed outside the fortress, the [[Captain of the Guard]],<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> [[Ziton Moj]], greeted them upon their arrival. With both Maul and Moj backed by large amounts of soldiers, the renegade Sith requested a meeting with the Black Sun's leaders, which Moj agreed to. The syndicate was headed by<ref name="Eminence" /> the Falleen [[Xomit Grunseit]], who hailed from Mustafar.<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''</ref> After negotiations with the leaders went sour, Savage beheaded all of them with his [[Savage Opress's lightsaber|lightsaber]]. Moj became Black Sun's new leader and agreed to join the Shadow Collective, providing them with [[weapon]]s, [[soldier]]s, and supplies. Shadow Collective forces then began to load all of the supplies the Black Sun had at their disposal onto ships.<ref name="Eminence" />

=====The lost children=====
{{Quote|Ah, yes, scenic Mustafar, because everyone looks good in red lighting. Become a bounty hunter, see the galaxy!|Quinlan Vos, to Asajj Ventress|<ref name="Dark Disciple" />}}
[[File:BlackSunfortressMustafar.png|thumb|right|300px|Quinlan Vos and Asajj Ventress were hired by the Pykes to conduct a rescue mission at Black Sun's headquarters.]]
When [[Quinlan Vos]] was sent undercover as a bounty hunter to work alongside Dooku's former apprentice, [[Asajj Ventress]], the pair was hired by the [[Pyke Syndicate]] to [[Rescue of Marg Krim's family|retrieve]] [[Marg Krim]]'s wife, [[Tezzka Krim]], and their children, [[Vram (Pyke)|Vram]] and [[Laalee]], who were kidnapped by Black Sun and brought to their base on Mustafar in order to bribe the [[Pyke]]s into joining Maul's Shadow Collective. The two traveled to Mustafar in Ventress' ship, the [[Banshee (starship)|''Banshee'']], and entered [[Zitontown]], where they sought to gather information at the lone bar in the town, named [[The Last Resort]]. Inside, the pair interrogated a [[Unidentified Black Sun guard|Falleen Black Sun enforcer]] and discovered where the [[prisoner]]s were held. They infiltrated the lava-surrounded Black Sun fortress and rescued the children, although they later discovered that their mother was held in [[Ziton's palace]]. After the pair freed Tezzka, Moj had mobilized his forces for departure from Mustafar to attack the Pykes on the planet [[Oba Diah]].<ref name="Dark Disciple" />

====Mirror of the soul====
=====The obviated war=====
{{Quote|After you have killed all the Jedi in the Temple, go to the Mustafar system. Wipe out Viceroy Gunray and the other Separatist leaders. Once more the Sith will rule the galaxy, and we shall have peace…|Darth Sidious to his new apprentice, Darth Vader|audio=Sidious-we-shall-have-peace.flac|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:KleggerCorpMiningFacility.png|thumb|left|320px|The Mustafarian mining complex that served as the Separatist Council's refuge at the war's end.]]
As the war's end drew nearer, Darth Sidious instructed the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] to retreat to their facility on Mustafar, and they gathered at the Techno Union's Klegger Corp Mining Facility under the leadership of [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]. Soon afterward, the Jedi Anakin Skywalker made a [[Duel in Palpatine's office|pact]] with Sidious, becoming his new Sith apprentice, [[Darth]] Vader; the Jedi-turned-Sith was desperately hoping to gain the power to save his lover and [[Marriage|wife]], Republic [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], from dying. Darth Vader's first mission was to [[Mission to Mustafar|eliminate]] Separatist leaders on Mustafar.<ref name="ROTS" />

Traveling from the Republic [[capital]] world of Coruscant in his [[Darth Vader's green Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor|interceptor]] alongside his [[Astromech droid|droid]] [[R2-D2]], Vader arrived at the Separatist facility's war room and promptly slaughtered the Separatist Council and their guards, bathing in the power of the dark side. At his [[Sith Master|master's]] command, Vader further transmitted the order to deactivate the [[Separatist Droid Army]] immediately, effectively ending the Clone Wars. At the same time, the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic|clone army]] was ordered to kill all Jedi, and Darth Sidious took the opportunity to [[Proclamation of the New Order|found]] the [[Galactic Empire]] with himself as the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]], fulfilling the Sith [[Grand Plan]] with his aim to seize control of the galaxy.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Lefranieclipse.png|thumb|right|320px|Lefrani eclipses Mustafar's sun, just after Darth Vader's massacre of the Separatists.]]
A rumor spread over the fire plains of Mustafar that a Jedi Knight—a reputed protector of light, guardian of peace and life, and a hero of the Republic—had been spotted at the Mining Complex. The Mustafarian boy [[Kakan]] hoped to exact his dream of meeting a Jedi, and so approached the fallen Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> The Sith Lord was viewing<ref name="ROTS" /> the eclipse of Mustafar's sun by Lefrani at the complex's balcony, just as Vader's massacre of the Separatists eclipsed the light of the Force within him.<ref name="CL" />

However, Kakan saw that the figure was not the Jedi he expected. The fallen Jedi's eyes radiated such anger and hate that Kakan was compelled to run away, escaping to the complex's foundry. Kakan found the miner Lellis, who operated the facility's repulsor vents, releasing fumes from the depths of Mustafar that gave one illusions when inhaled. The potent fumes overwhelmed Vader with his fears, and Kakan and Lellis took advantage of his distraction to escape. However, as fear took hold of the boy as well, the two Mustafarians fell into a lava lake, but they were saved by a burst of Force energy released by Darth Vader in a bout of anger.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

=====To not let go=====
{{Quote|I hate you!|Darth Vader, to his former friend Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:DoctorAphra-30-HughesArt.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Battle of the heroes on Mustafar]]
Padmé Amidala had been rushing to Mustafar in the hope of saving her husband from falling further to the dark side. She arrived on the volcanic world shortly after the slaughter of the Separatist leaders, and Vader met her embrace at the Techno Union facility.<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> Her pleas fell on deaf ears, however, when Vader spotted his former [[Jedi Master]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], emerging from Amidala's [[J-type Naboo star skiff|ship]]. In his anger, Vader incorrectly assumed that his lover had betrayed him for Kenobi and [[Force choke|strangled]] her via the Force; Amidala thus realized that Anakin Skywalker had been consumed by his lust for power and was truly corrupted by the dark side.<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="CL" />

Darth Vader then gave his old master and former friend an ultimatum: either he was with him or against him. Plagued by self-doubt and his inability to let go of his assumptions, Vader [[Duel on Mustafar|attempted]] to slay Kenobi. As the two engaged in a [[lightsaber duel]], Vader bathed the remnants of his Jedi self in the dark side that echoed from Mustafar's Sith sanctum, and amid the chaos, the shields protecting the mining facility were shut down. Parts of the building as well as the ''[[Lapiz Cutter]]''—the late Nute Gunray's personal [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle|shuttle]]—were destroyed.<ref name="BMF54">{{BuildFalconCite|54|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref>

Forced to fight across the lava streams, Vader was fueled by hatred and, in his hubris, attacked without regard to his own limitations. He fell victim to Kenobi's [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|blade]] beside a lava river. As the Sith Lord lost himself to the dark side's corruption, his remaining limbs were severed and his entire body was incinerated by Mustafar's lava.<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="CL" />

=====Scarring legacies=====
{{Quote|Do not underestimate how much you disappointed me on Mustafar. I saved you—but you showed how far off the mark you fell…|Darth Sidious, to Darth Vader|<ref name="DV6">[[Darth Vader (2015) 6|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 6]]</ref>}}
[[File:Let_The_Hate_Flow_AtG.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Sidious rescues his apprentice after he was left for dead on Mustafar's sands by Kenobi.]]
The fallen Jedi's [[Skywalker lightsaber|lightsaber]] was then taken by Kenobi, who left him to die on the sands<ref name="ROTS gallery">{{SW|url=films/star-wars-episode-3-revenge-of-the-sith-story-gallery|text=''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' Story Gallery}} {{C|Slide 47}}</ref> of the river bank. Kenobi then took Amidala to a [[Polis Massa Base|base]] on the [[asteroid field]] [[Polis Massa]] in order for her to give birth to her and Anakin Skywalker's children—the twins [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]] and [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia]]. Although charred and broken, Vader was recovered by Sidious, and he was brought back to Coruscant to be rebuilt with [[cybernetics]] at<ref name="ROTS" /> the [[Grand Republic Medical Facility]]<ref name="CL" /> with the technology of the acclaimed [[scientist]] [[Cylo]],<ref name="DV20">[[Darth Vader (2015) 20|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 20]]</ref> becoming encased in a [[Darth Vader's armor|suit]] of terrifying black [[armor]].<ref name="USWNE" />

Despite his survival, the events of Mustafar haunted Darth Vader throughout the age of the Empire, affecting the Sith's performance as the Emperor's<ref name="DV20" /><ref name="Aphra 40">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 40|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 40]]</ref> primary enforcer.<ref name="SithSWE">{{SWE|groups|sith|Sith}}</ref> Seldomly, stories circulated amongst Mustafarians of a great Jedi duel on their world, although no evidence was given for such tales.<ref name="SM" /> Mustafarians nonetheless had knowledge of the former Jedi who slaughtered the Separatist leaders and nearly killed the boy Kakan and the miner Lellis, and whilst some thought that the fallen Jedi Knight was gone, others thought that he still remained in the mists of Mustafar. Years later, Lellis realized that Darth Vader was the very same fallen Jedi Knight, overshadowing his people since the rise of the Empire.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

Over a year after the battle against his former friend on Mustafar, in [[18 BBY]],<ref name="Ahsoka date">The early chapters of the novel [[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] state that its events take place one [[Standard year|year]] after the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Proclamation of the New Order|founding]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' states was concurrent to the [[duel on Mustafar]], dated to [[19 BBY]]. Therefore, the later chapters of ''Ahsoka'' take place more than a year after the duel, in [[18 BBY]].</ref> the memory of Darth Vader burning on the volcanic slopes of Mustafar resurfaced in Obi-Wan Kenobi's thoughts along with other past happenings. Despite the pain inflicted by the memories, Kenobi willed himself to let go of his traumatic past and focus on his present—his mission to watch over Luke, the son of Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="Ahsoka">[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]</ref>

===Vader's domain (19–9 BBY)===
====Sanctum of the Sith====
{{Quote|When you arrive on Mustafar, find the place where the dark side calls to you. Draw upon the energy there—combine its power with your own. Then… use it.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Vader|<ref name="DV5" />}}
[[File:VaderBleeding-2017DarthVader5.jpg|thumb|left|320px|Vader bled his new kyber crystal until it shone crimson.]]
A short time after his loss to Kenobi, in 19 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> Vader returned to Mustafar under instructions from Darth Sidious. Vader was to [[Bleeding|bleed]] a kyber crystal he had obtained from the Jedi Master [[Kirak Infil'a]], who he killed, in order to gain a crimson [[crystal]] for his new [[Sith lightsaber]]. He traveled to the dark side cave<ref name="DV5" /> that contained the shrine erected by the ancient Sith<ref name="TROS VD" /> and poured all of his pain and anger into the crystal, making it sing a hymn of darkness. With this new [[Kirak Infil'a's lightsaber|weapon]], Vader returned to Coruscant by his master's side, another step closer, Sidious believed, to becoming a true servant of darkness.<ref name="DV5" />

Although Sidious had lost his original facility during the Clone Wars,<ref name="Children of the Force" /> he soon built additional installations on Mustafar where he continued to abduct Force-sensitive infants. Over time, he manipulated these children and molded them into new members of the [[Inquisitorius]],<ref name="BuildR2 33">{{BuildR2Cite|33|Droid Directory}}</ref> a group of dark side [[Jedi hunter|agents]] trained by Darth Vader and initially made up of former Jedi, including [[the Grand Inquisitor]], since soon after the Empire's founding.<ref name="DV7">[[Darth Vader (2017) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 7]]</ref>

In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Vader captured the former Jedi [[Chief Librarian]] [[Jocasta Nu]], a survivor of the [[Great Jedi Purge|Jedi Purge]] at the end of the Clone Wars, and obtained a [[memory crystal]] given to Nu by [[Jedi seeker]]s who identified potential [[Jedi Initiate]]s from throughout the galaxy—it listed the names and locations of many Force-sensitives, including the individual [[Nik Lowe]] on Mustafar. Wary that the Emperor could replace him with another Force user, Vader murdered Nu and destroyed the memory crystal.<ref name="DV10">[[Darth Vader (2017) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 10]]</ref>

After the [[Chiss]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] "Thrawn" came into contact with the Empire in 14 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> having been attacked by a talented trio of [[Imperial cadet|cadets]] when he was studying at Coruscant's prestigious [[Royal Imperial Academy]], Thrawn recommended to [[Commandant]] [[Deenlark]] that his assailants be transferred away. When a derisive Deenlark asked if they should be transferred to Mustafar as punishment, Thrawn suggested that the three train instead as [[starfighter]] [[pilot]]s at<ref name="Thrawn">[[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']]</ref> the elite [[Skystrike Academy]] on the world [[Montross]].<ref name="Skystrike Academy">{{Databank|skystrike-academy|Skystrike Academy}}</ref>

====Vader's plans====
{{Quote|You created this design, in your last body. Tell me what it is.''"<br />"''The door to the dark side is locked. This is the key. Your beloved waits for you there, Vader. My fortress will tune the energies of the locus. It is your first step towards using the power of the dark side to pierce the veil of time, between life and death.|Darth Vader and Momin, on the design of Fortress Vader|<ref name="DV22">[[Darth Vader (2017) 22|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 22]]</ref>}}
[[File:MustafariansVsVader-2017DarthVader22.png|thumb|right|350px|Darth Vader wields his new crimson blade against Mustafarians, who were less than welcoming of their new neighbor.]]
Fascinated by the power he tapped into in the Sith cave on Mustafar,<ref name="DV21" /> and associating the world with his rebirth and personal connection to the dark side,<ref name="USWNE" /> Vader requested that the world be given to him by his master<ref name="DV21" /> in 14 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> believing that the planet held the key to seeing the deceased Padmé Amidala once again. Gifted with the late Amidala's [[Naboo Royal Starship|royal starship]], the [[Mask of Lord Momin|mask]] of the ancient Sith heretic artisan [[Darth Momin]], and a team of top Imperial [[architect]]s, Vader departed Coruscant for his new home. The Sith Lord entered the planet's violent atmosphere unshielded, causing severe damage to his vessel and casting a streak of fire across the smokey sky. His entry was witnessed by the Mustafarian [[Father (title)|Father]] [[Kkkt]], who warned his [[Kkkt's clan|clanmate]] [[Zzzs]] that the fireball was an omen of events to come.<ref name="DV21" />

Landing near the Sith cave, Vader [[Meditation|meditated]] in its dark walls, leaving the Emperor's architects, [[Colonel]] [[Alva Brenne]] and [[Lieutenant]] [[Roggo]], to draw up plans for a personal base Vader could inhabit. Brenne [[scout]]ed the planet's terrain, believing that, although Vader was seemingly impossible to satisfy, she could manage to design a home suitable for the Dark Lord. Unbeknownst to the architects, the mask that Sidious had gifted Vader was [[Possession|possessed]] by Darth Momin's spirit; it took control of Roggo, using his body to kill Brenne and create its own designs for the base.<ref name="DV21" />

[[File:VaderMeditatesInCave-2017DarthVader21.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Vader meditates in the Sith cave.]]
Vader confronted the spirit, killing its host body and demanding that it gives him answers. The spirit introduced itself as Momin and offered to help Vader construct a fortress that would harness the energies<ref name="DV21" /> of the dark side locus below the cave to open a door into the Force itself;<ref name="USWNE" /> through and beyond the limitations of [[time]] and space.<ref name="DV21" /> Upon being [[Skirmish on Mustafar|attacked]] by Father Kkkt's scout party, Vader abducted the Mustafarian [[Sssp]] to serve as Momin's new body and let [[Rrrn]] flee. The two Sith Lords subsequently took command of a vast Imperial construction force on the Gahenn Plains and began their work on what would become [[Fortress Vader]].<ref name="DV22" />

Vader would exercise control over the entire Mustafar system.<ref name="Kenobi IV">{{Kenobi|Part IV}}</ref> Around this time, the Inquisitorius' headquarters were moved from Coruscant to the moon [[Nur]] in the Mustafar system, keeping close to Vader and his planet.<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> A base<ref name="Kenobi IV" /> but also a clandestine place of [[Prison|incarceration]] and [[torture]] for Jedi,<ref name="JFO">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]''</ref> the [[Fortress Inquisitorius]] tower was built to complement the castle on Mustafar using black stone from the world<ref name="Dawn">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> in 14 BBY.<ref name="Timelines" />

====Portal to the past====
{{Quote|I have been in contact with the other clanholds. We are not the only one affected—the entire planet screams at what the dark one is building on the Gahenn Plains.|Father Kkkt|<ref name="DV23" />}}
[[File:FortressVaderLightning-2017DarthVader23.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Momin's imperfect designs caused chaos on Mustafar.]]
The construction of Vader's fortress was not a simple task. Over the course of eight attempts<ref name="USWNE" /> with at least five separate designs, Momin struggled to find the perfect structure that could correctly channel the dark side. The energy Vader exerted while attempting to open a rift in the locus caused electromagnetic storms to rage across the planet, throwing the world's creatures into a frenzy and casting the Mustafarian people into disarray—the natives found that their "lifefires" barely burned. As an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] loomed overhead, the new [[Fortress Vader Imperial garrison|Imperial garrison]] managed to defend the site against small uprisings by the Mustafarians and lava fleas. Father Kkkt, realizing the danger Vader posed to his world, rallied the clanholds across Mustafar prepared to mount an [[Battle of Fortress Vader|attack]] on the Imperial intruders.<ref name="DV23" />

Upon the completion of Momin's ninth design<ref name="DV23" /> in [[12 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Vader was finally able to reach through the Force and open a [[Portal|pathway into time]], but he was interrupted in his moment of triumph by Kkkt and his forces. With the Dark Lord distracted, Momin entered the portal and claimed his original body, betraying Vader.<ref name="DV23" /> Kkkt's army had initial success in pushing back [[Captain]] [[Junus]]' garrison, attacking the Imperials, whom they outnumbered by ten to one, with surprise tactics. Vader, however, soon arrived on the front lines and rallied his [[magma trooper]]s to double their efforts. Recognizing Vader as the Imperial leader, Kkkt led the Mustafarians in a powerful [[Telekinesis|usage of the Force]], drowning the enemy forces in a vast flood of lava. With his army wiped out, Vader retreated into the fortress, summoning his own massive force of energy to destroy the Mustafarian attackers.<ref name="DV24">[[Darth Vader (2017) 24|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 24]]</ref>

[[File:SithCavePortal-2017DarthVader25.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Vader enters the portal in the Sith cave.]]
Returning to the inner sanctum, Vader confronted Momin, who mocked the [[cyborg]] Sith for his failures in service to the dark side. Using Momin's hubris against him, Vader crushed and killed the resurrected artist. With no one to stop him, he entered the portal,<ref name="DV24" /> encountering visions of his past and future, including his beloved wife, Padmé Amidala. Upon witnessing what her husband had become, however, the vision of Amidala ran from Vader, choosing to plunge into an abyss. A beam of light containing a figure that he did not know was his son then overwhelmed Vader.<ref name="DV25">[[Darth Vader (2017) 25|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 25]]</ref> Frustrated with the dark visions, Vader retreated and crushed the altar in the Sith cave, destroying the portal<ref name="USWNE" /> and accepting that the truth he encountered was exactly what he needed.<ref name="DV25" /> The Dark Lord later returned Momin's mask to Sidious;<ref name="Encyclopedia Maul">{{EncyclopediaCite|Darth Maul and Other Followers of the Dark Side}}</ref> both master and apprentice frequented Mustafar, using it to focus their meditation on the power of the dark side of the Force.<ref name="CL" />

====Mustafarian revolts====
{{Quote|This is an ''Imperial'' facility.''"<br />"''And this is ''our'' world. A world with secrets that I have vowed to protect at all costs.|Rersey and Sssl|<ref name="Return 5" />}}
Black Sun departed Mustafar to a lower profile world after the Empire had established a garrison there.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The Techno Union similarly abandoned their operations, and their remaining resources were taken over by the Mining Guild, but they struggled to profit on Mustafar due to the strict travel restrictions imposed by the Empire.<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> The Empire replenished their garrison<ref name="Tales 5" /> and maintained secret facilities on Mustafar where survivors of the Jedi Purge were interrogated and [[Death penalty|executed]], although the lava planet remained publicly notable only for its mining operations.<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> Rumor had it that Darth Vader carried out these interrogations, torturing the Jedi for any useful information before their execution.<ref name="Aftermath">[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']]</ref> As the world remained under heavy Imperial guard, mining operations there eventually ceased.<ref name="Tales 1">[[Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle 1|''Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle'' 1]]</ref>

In [[11 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> the term "[[Mustafarian Special]]" was used by [[smuggler]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] and his [[First Mate|first mate]], [[L3-37]], to refer to a [[starfighter]] maneuver that involved great speed and surprise, and which ensured at least one side of a [[Starfighter combat|starship confrontation]] "end[ed] badly." L3-37 explained that the tactic was named such in reference to the eponymous lava world's fiery nature.<ref name="Lando's Luck" />

[[File:VaneeMaster-ShadowOfVadersCastle.jpg|thumb|right|350px|According to a tale, an Imperial officer was driven insane by Mustafar's lava fumes and became Vader's servant Vaneé.]]
Following Kkkt's failed attack and the completion of Fortress Vader<ref name="Tales 5" />—according to a story told years later by the Mustafarian Lellis—Darth Vader sought candidates for a [[Aide|servant]] who would attend to his needs, searching for [[Standard month|months]] until a human named [[Vaneé]] came into his service<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> around 12 BBY.<ref name="Timelines" /> During Vader's search, an [[Imperial officer]] was sent from [[Imperial High Command|Imperial Command]] to Mustafar by [[Moff]] [[Seward]], and was tasked with handling an outbreak of insanity amongst Imperial [[Volcanic environment stormtrooper|lava troopers]] assigned to Fortress Vader. On Mustafar, the inspector found that the [[trooper]]s had inhaled toxic fumes from the planet's depths that gave one illusions of fears and doubts, and he entered Vader's castle to speak with Darth Vader himself with the intention of resolving the matter. However, Vader, bathing in his [[bacta tank]], instead forced the officer to inhale the fumes and confront his fears by holding him in place via the Force, refusing to let the human go. Face with the illusions caused by the Mustafarian fumes, the inspector denied their existence and began to laugh, laughing for days until he took advice from the voices by his head and became Vader's servant, named Vaneé.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

Eventually, years before the [[Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> of [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> the lava fumes leaking into Vader's castle were blocked off.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> During the early days of Vader's reign over the planet, Vaneé witnessed the efforts of a second force of Mustafarians to push the Sith away from their homeworld. The group, led by [[Criakan]], desired vengeance for their slaughtered kin and [[Raid on Fortress Vader|stormed]] the fortress in a surprise attack. Surrounding Vaneé, Criakan and his forces intended to show no mercy to the Imperials, but were shown the same respect by Lord Vader, who cut them all down before they could burn down the castle.<ref name="Tales 5" />

[[File:ThirdAttackOnFortressVader-ReturnToVadersCastle5.png|thumb|left|350px|Darth Vader fights Priestess Sssl's forces at Fortress Vader.]]
Sometime later, during a visit from the [[Emperor's adviser]] [[Rersey]], a third [[attack on Fortress Vader]] was undertaken by [[Clan Rrrt]]'s [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Sssl]], a Mustafarian [[priestess]] who could force her will upon others by subjecting them to a [[Unidentified plague (Mustafar)|mind-altering plague]]. Sssl's forces soon overwhelmed the Imperials, infecting Vader's soldiers and turning them against the Sith. Although Sssl had only intended to scare off the invaders, her plans changed when the Dark Lord himself was seemingly infected. In reality, Vader's mechanical body was immune to the plague, allowing him to feign subservience and draw the priestess out. Using a [[mind trick]], Vader forced Sssl to order her own forces to drag her into the lava—a scene that made Rersey lose his sanity. Vaneé praised his master and noted that the Mustafarians would fear Vader's name in the future.<ref name="Return 5" />

===Galactic war on Mustafar (9 BBY–1 ABY)===
====Rebels in peril====
{{Quote|Yes the naval action at Mustafar was a short-term win. But the Empire now knows the measure of the Alliance's naval strength.|Mon Mothma, ''The Rebel Files''|<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>}}
In [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Darth Vader conferred from Fortress Vader with the [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]] via [[hologram]] regarding their [[hunt for Obi-Wan]] following a [[Search for Princess Leia|failed attempt]] to capture him.<ref name="Kenobi III">{{Kenobi|Part III}}</ref> Kenobi later [[Rescue of Princess Leia (9 BBY)|infiltrated]] Fortress Inquisitorius on the nearby moon Nur using intelligence from the [[Hidden Path]] rebels, who further found that Vader was not in the Mustafar system at the time, instead being aboard his [[Devastator|vessel]] elsewhere.<ref name="Kenobi IV" /> The hunt was ultimately a failure, and from his castle, Vader was instructed by Darth Sidious via hologram to abandon his obsession with Kenobi.<ref name="Kenobi VI">{{Kenobi|Part VI}}</ref>

[[File:Imperial_Mustafar.jpg|thumb|right|320px|Imperial Star Destroyers stood watch over Mustafar.]]
In [[4 BBY]],<ref name="GA" /> the Jedi [[Kanan Jarrus]] of the rebel cell named the [[Spectres]] was detained aboard the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer]] ''[[Sovereign]]'', the [[flagship]] of [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Grand Moff]]<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> and [[Governor]] of the Outer Rim.<ref name="AEYNK" /> The vessel entered Mustafar's orbit<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> after the Empire's [[Raid on the communications tower|capture]] of the Jedi on the Outer Rim planet [[Lothal]], where the Spectres were based.<ref name="Call to Action">{{Rebels|Call to Action}}</ref> Escorted by a [[Imperial Navy|fleet]] of three other [[Star Destroyer]]s and support vessels, the ''Sovereign'' bore witness to the [[Grand Inquisitor]]'s interrogation of Jarrus for information about the rebellion and the informant named "[[Fulcrum]]"<ref name="Mustafar DB" />—who was secretly the [[Force-Sensitive Outcast|former Jedi]] Ahsoka Tano. [[Hera Syndulla]] led her Spectres crew on a [[Action at Mustafar|rescue mission]] over Mustafar. Using a stolen [[Evac One|Imperial Gozanti-class cruiser]] and [[Rebels TIE fighter|TIE fighter]] to infiltrate the ''Sovereign'', the Spectres freed their captive Jedi from the Grand Inquisitor. The latter's [[The Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber|lightsaber]] was bisected during lightsaber combat against Jarrus and his Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]], and fell into the ''Sovereign''{{'s}} [[Solar ionization reactor|reactor]], dooming the Star Destroyer. The Inquisitor himself chose to fall to his death rather than suffer for his failures.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy">{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}}</ref>

With the aid of [[Phoenix Cell]], a resistance group affiliated with "Fulcrum" in a growing network of rebels formed by Senators [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] and [[Mon Mothma]],<ref name="Rebel Files" /> the Spectres successfully fled the Mustafar system and joined the larger Phoenix Cell. Grand Moff Tarkin also evacuated from his flagship,<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> which crashed into Mustafar's lava fields<ref name="AEYNK" /> in a defeat that embarrassed Tarkin and displeased Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="Epic Battles">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Visual Guide: Epic Battles]]''</ref> The skirmish over Mustafar marked one of the earliest rebel victories in the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the Empire<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> and heightened rebellious activity in the Outer Rim,<ref name="AlderaanCruiser">{{Databank|alderaan-cruiser|Alderaan Cruiser}}</ref> with unrest occuring on Lothal that [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] attributed to some [[Lothalite]]s perceiving the Empire as vulnerable following rumors of the Empire's show of weakness at Mustafar.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> Mon Mothma wrote in documents assembled in ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' that the action at Mustafar was but a short-term success, considering that the rebels had revealed the naval capacity of their sector fleet to the Empire.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> Indeed, the Emperor sent Darth Vader to personally handle the rebel group.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" />

Having become a part of Bail Organa's rebel network, Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger began working with their fellow rebel Force-sensitive, Ahsoka Tano.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> In 3 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> Tano reached out to Jarrus with report of her investigation on the Sith Lord who [[Siege of Lothal|attacked]] them over the planet [[Lothal]] shortly prior—unbeknownst to them, he was Darth Vader<ref name="The Future of the Force">{{Rebels|The Future of the Force}}</ref> and formerly the Jedi Anakin Skywalker, who instructed Tano.<ref name="Timelines" /> She had been monitoring transmissions from Mustafar, and while information on the Sith Lord remained elusive, she had gathered more intelligence on the Empire's Inquisitors. The former Jedi decoded two sets of coordinates from the Mustafar transmissions, and after she learned of an incident above the planet [[Chandel]], she and the Spectres investigated the world [[Takobo]], where they uncovered the Inquisitors' plot to kidnap Force-sensitive infants.<ref name="The Future of the Force" /> Tano recalled that it was similar to the kidnapping attempt that she and her master had foiled on Mustafar during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Children of the Force" />

In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> based on intelligence about the Empire's operations on Mustafar, a small [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] force was sent by Captain [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] to infiltrate an [[Imperial base (Mustafar)|Imperial base]] located near Vader's castle and steal a vital artifact. Upon infiltrating the base, the rebels discovered the artifact was a [[proto-saber]], a precursor to the lightsaber, and escaped with information about the ancient weapon despite Vader's intervention.<ref name="Secrets">''[[Star Wars: Secrets of the Empire]]''</ref>

====Legacy of Corvax====
{{Quote|Whoa. Whoa, that looks like—that looks like Mustafar. Mustafar's a mining planet. Why are the Imperials taking us there?|ZO-E3, to her captain|<ref name="Immortal 1" />}}
[[File:Windfall_above_Mustafar.jpg|thumb|left|260px|A smuggler and ZO-E3 arrive at Mustafar.]]
In the same year,<ref name="Timelines" /> while Mustafar maintained its reputation as a mining world, a [[Corvax descendant|smuggler]] and [[ZO-E3]] aboard the ''[[Windfall]]'' were forcefully taken to Mustafar, having been taken out of [[hyperspace]] in the Mustafar system by an [[Interdictor-class Star Destroyer|''Interdictor''-class]] Star Destroyer commanded by [[Admiral]] [[Gable Karius]].<ref name="Immortal 1" /> Karius served Vader as his second-in-command on Mustafar,<ref name="Karius">{{Databank|admiral-karius|Admiral Karius}}</ref> and the smuggler and ZO-E3 were held in Vader's castle. The Sith Lord then interrogated the smuggler, realizing that they had a strong connection to the Force and was a descendant of Lady Corvax. However, they then escaped below the castle to the underground Corvax Fortress, meeting the Mustafarian [[Priestess (Mustafarian)|Priestess]] and activating [[Marching Horde|Lady Corvax's droid army]] to [[Battle on Mustafar|attack]] the Imperials.<ref name="Immortal 1" />

Darth Vader briefly taught the Corvax descendant to harness the power of the Force in order to retrieve the Bright Star artifact, wishing to revive Padmé Amidala with it.<ref name="Immortal 2" /> The Sith Lord was prevented from doing so by the descendant, who staged an escape from the fortress and destroyed the Bright Star and the Aeon Engine, allowing Mustafar to begin restoring its forested ecosystems.<ref name="Immortal 3" /> Near Fortress Vader, the fertile soil grounds of<ref name="TROS VD" /> a bog named Corvax Fen began developing.<ref name="Inside Intel" />

====Crushing aspirations====
{{Quote|You seem unsettled.''"<br />"''No…just pressed for time.|Lord Vader and Director Krennic|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
[[File:Vaders-shadow.png|thumb|right|300px|Orson Krennic arrives at Fortress Vader.]]
Later still in the year,<ref name="Timelines" /> the Empire completed construction on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], an orbital [[battle station]] capable of destroying a planet. After a [[Mission to Eadu|rebel attack]] on a [[Eadu Energy Conversion Laboratory|laboratory]] on the world [[Eadu]] threatened to expose the Death Star's capabilities to the galaxy at large,<ref name="Rogue One" /> Vader summoned the [[director]] of the project, [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]], to his fortress on Mustafar.<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> Krennic, arriving while Vader was sustained within a [[bacta]] tank,<ref name="Rogue One" /> was escorted into Fortress Vader's rotunda by Vaneé to await the Dark Lord. Confronting the uneasy director, Vader admonished Krennic for his mistakes, using the Force to choke the aspirational officer when he further requested an audience with the Emperor. With his message relayed,<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> Vader watched Krennic's ship depart<ref name="RO Adaptation 4">[[Rogue One Adaptation 4|''Rogue One Adaptation'' 4]]</ref> for the planet [[Scarif]].<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> Despite Vader's threats, Krennic failed in his endeavors<ref name="Rogue One" /> and the Death Star was soon destroyed by the Rebel Alliance. Around the same time, the rebels also destroyed the Empire's [[Mirkanite Mining Facility]] on Mustafar.<ref name="BMF 17" />

Later in the war, a [[Lina Graf's crew|crew]] of rebels led by [[Commander]] [[Lina Graf]] was [[Fact-finding mission to the Outer Rim|attacked]] by Imperial forces, and their ship, the ''[[Auric]]'', was heavily damaged. They were forced to crash-land on Mustafar, a planet that Graf hoped would lead to her crew's salvation. Surrounded by lava, the rebels abandoned their ship and began toward the only structure in sight; Vader's fortress.<ref name="Tales 1" />

They did not make it far before being attacked by Mustafar's exploding beetles. After defeating the beetles and arguing over the best course of action, Graf and her crew were cornered by a [[squad]] of Imperial Lava Troopers.<ref name="Tales 2" /> Escaping the troopers, the group entered the fortress but soon became separated in its dark halls. Alerted to their presence by his aide Vaneé, Vader confronted the rebels,<ref name="Tales 4">[[Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle 4|''Star Wars Adventures: Tales from Vader's Castle'' 4]]</ref> capturing [[Lieutenant]] [[Thom Hudd]]<ref name="Return 1" /> and destroying the [[bodyguard droid]] [[XM-G3]],<ref name="Tales 4" /> although Graf and her remaining crew managed to escape Mustafar.<ref name="Tales 5" /> The rebels' successful escape from Vader's castle was remembered by the native Mustafarians by the aftermath of the Empire's collapse.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

[[File:AuricCrashesOnMustafar-TalesFromVadersCastle1.png|thumb|left|250px|The ''Auric'' crashes on Mustafar.]]
For the next several [[Standard week|weeks]],<ref name="Return 4">[[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle 4|''Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle'' 4]]</ref> Vaneé kept Hudd locked within the fortress and tortured him, all the while tormenting him with horrific tales from across the galaxy,<ref name="Return 3">[[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle 3|''Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle'' 3]]</ref> including the story of Vader's brutal murder of Sssl years prior.<ref name="Return 5" /> The abuse and starvation that Hudd suffered while chained to the Sith servant's [[torture web]] was so severe that he lost enough body mass to slip from his shackles and escape his cell.<ref name="Return 3" /> Hudd managed to send a [[distress signal]] to the Alliance but was ultimately recaptured and sentenced to death. His execution was stalled by Graf, however, who had [[Mission to Fortress Vader|returned]] to Mustafar disguised as an [[Fourth Sister|Inquisitor]]. Although Vaneé saw through her ruse, Graf and Hudd were able to escape and flee the planet with the rest of their crew. Vader, angered at his servant's ineptitude, rigged Vaneé up to the torture web.<ref name="Return 5" />

The loss of the Death Star served to galvanize resistance across the galaxy, causing trouble for the weakened Empire. In response to the outbreak of rebellion, Vader was met at Fortress Vader by Admiral [[Kendal Ozzel]] and [[General]] [[Maximilian Veers]]. Overlooking Mustafar's lava fields, the trio discussed the proper route to deal with the rising Alliance, although Vader viewed Ozzel's suggestions as nothing more than excuses for incompetency. An interesting point from General Veers, however, persuaded Vader to view the rebels in a new light, prompting him to develop a different plan to [[Battle of Mako-Ta|cripple]] the Alliance.<ref name="Shu-Torun Lives">{{StoryCite|story=Shu-Torun Lives|book=Star Wars (2015) 50}}</ref>

===Crucible of fate and hate (3–4 ABY)===
====Into the fire====
{{Quote|The last time you were ''broken''…I ''found'' you…and I ''rebuilt'' you. This time… you must rebuild yourself.|Palpatine, to his battered apprentice|<ref name="Vader 2020 6">[[Darth Vader (2020) 6|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 6]]</ref>}}
[[File:HeBurnsAgain-2020DarthVader6.png|thumb|right|240px|Vader was mutilated and burned just as he was at the end of the Clone Wars.]]
In [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Vader attempted to turn his son, Luke Skywalker, to the dark side during a [[Duel on Cloud City|duel]] over the planet [[Bespin]]. After Skywalker [[Escape from Cloud City|fled]], Vader temporarily abandoned his duties to the Emperor, embarking on a personal quest that led to the discovery of a [[Amidalans|rebel cell]] led by [[Sabé]], the former [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|decoy]] of Padmé Amidala. Vader allowed the rebels to live, a decision which convinced Sidious that his apprentice was in need of a reminder of his place.
