The Emperor mutilated Vader on Coruscant, ripping his cybernetic limbs from his body and strangling him as he had done to men like Krennic in the past.<ref name="Vader 2020 6" />

Not finished with his lesson, Sidious took his student back to Mustafar. He had Vader's [[Darth Vader's guard|personal guard]] of [[death trooper]]s drag him to the spot where Kenobi had defeated him decades ago, leaving the apprentice to fend for himself. Warned by his master that there would be consequences should he use the Force to save himself, a one-armed Vader crawled along the lava banks and retrieved his fallen lightsaber before slowly making his way to the ruins of the Techno Union installation. Sidious watched from Vader's [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class shuttle]] as the broken man pulled himself across the sand. Although [[Mas Amedda]], the Emperor's [[Grand Vizier]], warned that the Dark Lord planned to kill his master, Sidious was unconcerned and sent his [[Sith assassin]], [[Ochi|Ochi of Bestoon]], to turn Vader's anger into pain.<ref name="Vader 2020 6" />

[[File:VaderEyeOfWebbishBog-Revelations2022.png|thumb|left|320px|Darth Vader meets with the Eye of Webbish Bog.]]
Having reached the Techno Union installation ruins, the very building where he had slaughtered the Separatist Council decades prior, Vader repurposed surrounding Separatist droid parts as his own limbs and confronted Ochi, overpowering the assassin and demanding him to reveal Darth Sidious' plans. As Vader did so, the oracle [[Eye of Webbish Bog]] called out to the Sith Lord,<ref name="Vader 2020 7">[[Darth Vader (2020) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 7]]</ref> who, despite being deprived of his chest box and [[Darth Vader's lightsaber|lightsaber]] by Ochi, fought his way through hordes of lava nymphs, lava fleas, and even a roggwart to reach the Eye's lava cavern. As Vader did so, he was tested by the Eye and reminded of his inner conflicts between his chosen Sith and Jedi destinies as well as between his personal desire of power and his need for his son. During Vader's journey to the Eye's lair, [[Senior Administrative Aide]] [[Sly Moore]] and a group of death troopers spoke to Ochi, reminding the assassin to abide by the Emperor's directives.<ref name="Vader 2020 8">[[Darth Vader (2020) 8|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 8]]</ref>

At the end of Vader's trek to the Eye, the latter gave the cyborg a [[Vader's wayfinder|wayfinder]] and allowed him to leave the cavern to rejoin Ochi. Once outside, Vader made his way to the green Jedi starfighter that he took to Mustafar at the end of the Clone Wars,<ref name="Vader 2020 8" /> repairing the ship until Ochi reappeared with the [[Droid Crush Pirates of Bestoon]]. Having been promised Vader's cybernetic parts by Ochi, the army of droid pursued the Emperor's enforcer until they found that his parts were no more special than their own. In the midst of a quarrel with Ochi about their deal, the droids were interrupted by Vader, who took down the machines for use in retrofitting his green starfighter and an [[escape pod]], which he locked Ochi in after forcing the assassin to activate his wayfinder. In his determination to find the Emperor's secrets, Vader bound the pod to his starfighter and set off to the wayfinder's coordinates, reaching the [[Red Honeycomb Zone|vicinity]] of the [[Unknown Regions]] world [[Exegol]] via hyperspace.<ref name="Vader 2020 9">[[Darth Vader (2020) 9|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 9]]</ref>

[[File:ShipRepair-2020DarthVader9.png|thumb|right|275px|Darth Vader rebuilds his starfighter.]]
With Ochi in tow, Vader confronted Sidious on Exegol, an ancient Sith world which housed hundreds of Sidious' secret experiments and weapons. The Emperor reminded his wayward apprentice that he left him weak and broken on Mustafar's burning shores, and asked Vader what he learned from the experience. However, Vader remained rebellious, stating his intention to make his "master" fear him. Despite Vader's efforts, he was overwhelmed by Sidious' power. Terribly pained, Vader, despite having experienced a vision of his son telling him it was his destiny to destroy Sidious, accepted his master's dominance over him before leaving Exegol with him and Ochi.<ref name="Vader 2020 11">[[Darth Vader (2020) 11|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 11]]</ref>

====Crimson Dawn intrusion====
{{Quote|<nowiki />''Ha!'' You lose, ''chump!"<br />"Uh,'' boss, you sure that's such a good idea?|Ren, shouting at Vader, and a Knight of Ren|<ref name="CR 4" />}}
Later, between 3 ABY and 4 ABY,<ref name="Timelines" /> Lady [[Qi'ra]]'s criminal syndicate, [[Crimson Dawn]], hired the [[Knights of Ren]], a group of dark side warriors, to [[Heist on Vader's Castle|raid]] Fortress Vader and acquire the [[Screaming Key]] artifact<ref name="CR 4" />—Darth Sidious had placed the key there, but did not know that it unlocked Momin's fabled [[Fermata Cage]], which held power that threatened even the Sith.<ref name="HE 1">[[Hidden Empire 1|''Hidden Empire'' 1]]</ref> In her [[War against the Sith|quest]] to destroy the Sith, Qi'ra had obtained the full layout,<ref name="CR 4" /> access codes,<ref name="CR 1">[[Crimson Reign 4|''Crimson Reign'' 4]]</ref> and security details of the fortress and convinced the Knights' [[Ren|leader]], [[Ren (human)|Ren]], to go ahead with the raid despite initial reluctance from other Knights. The Knight [[Massif]] had complained that "the job was too hot" not just because Mustafar's surface was a hellscape, and fellow Knights [[Bazzra]] and [[Marinda]] also had their own concerns. Nevertheless, Qi'ra promised the Knights glory and the freedom to claim any objects to keep for themselves aside from the key.<ref name="CR 4" />

[[File:KnightsOfRenSithCave-CrimsonReign4.jpg|thumb|right|290px|The Knights of Ren enter Fortress Vader through the Sith cave.]]
The group landed their [[Oubliette-class transport|vessel]], the ''[[Night Buzzard]]'', on the Gahenn Plains and used [[speeder bike]]s to approach the fortress from the south. Ren had concluded that the sensors of the Imperial garrison on the building's far side could not detect them given Mustafar's magnetic field, and as they used their speeder's signal [[jammer]]s, they were able to approach undetected. The Knights approached an old entrance to the fortress that was covered by lava, but by using the Force to clear a way through, they entered the Sith cave below the installation. The helmet of Momin still lay in the cave, which spooked Bazzra into shooting and destroying it. They then continued on their route towards the vault.<ref name="CR 4" />

[[File:RenVaderDuel-CrimsonReign4.png|thumb|left|275px|Ren duels Darth Vader.]]
As they neared the vault, the Knights were spotted by Vaneé, who warned them that it was too late for them to turn back and that Vader would learn of their presence. The Knights turned their weapons on Vaneé, but he was protected by a force field. Meanwhile, a large group of lava troopers surrounded the Knights and a battle began. As the Knights fought their way to the vault, Ren began to cut open the door to the vault with [[Ren (lightsaber)|his lightsaber]]. Inside the vault, Ren used the Force to listen for the Screaming Key, and located the small gray key. Realizing that the battle had also gone quiet, Ren asked if they had defeated all the troopers, and while the Knights told him that they had all departed for unexplained reasons, Darth Vader emerged. Vader quickly killed the Knight [[Fyodor]] with a Force choke before Ren engaged him in lightsaber combat. As Vader and Ren traded blows, Vader learned that his opponents were the Knights of Ren. The remaining Knights fled at Ren's command, and Ren soon jumped out of a window to join them, using [[controlled descent]] to survive the fall. Vader attempted to use the Force to grab the key back out of Ren's hand, but the other Knights fired their blasters at Vader, forcing him to use his energy to deflect their shots. The Knights then fled on their speeders and left Mustafar with the key, which they delivered to Qi'ra's ally, [[The Archivist]], at a [[Dark side hellscape|location]] where The Archivist believed the Fermata Cage to be.<ref name="CR 4" />

====Scourge and Schism====
{{Quote|I have never been ''stronger''.|Darth Vader, training to focus his abilities on Mustafar|<ref name="DV202037">[[Darth Vader (2020) 37|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 37]]</ref>}}
The Eye of Webbish Bog called out to Vader, who entered his lair and experienced visions that the being hoped would serve as a warning to the Sith Lord of an impending culmination of interconnected galactic events. After receiving the visions, Vader found that the Eye was being poisoned by a device left in his cave and subsequently ambushed by several Mustafarians. The natives were unhappy with the Sith Lord's intrusion on their planet, but Vader dispatched them at the cost of only a scar left on his helmet and eliminated the device that had been plaguing the Eye. The Sith then returned to his castle, where he spoke with the Emperor via hologram about Lady Qi'ra's machinations against them.<ref name="Revelations">[[Revelations (2022) 1|''Revelations'' (2022) 1]]</ref>

After the Sith overcame Qi'ra's [[Battle at Amaxine Station|attempt]] to defeat them, Luke Skywalker communicated with a red kyber crystal on the planet [[Christophsis]], in the process experiencing a vision in which he saw Fortress Vader in the midst of a red lightning storm as well as his father, Darth Vader.<ref name="2020SW35">[[Star Wars (2020) 35|''Star Wars'' (2020) 35]]</ref> Qi'ra's activation of the Fermata Cage during her war against the Sith had [[Force Wave|destabilized]] Vader's mastery of the Force, and the Dark Lord, wielding the [[Zaly Shield]] alongside a [[Darth Vader's electrostaff|staff]], returned to the lava fields before his castle to train himself in focusing his powers.<ref name="DV202037" /> Meanwhile, the [[Scourge]], a droid-possessing [[Scourge crisis|malady]], intended to control Vader as he was a cyborg who could use the Force. It arrived on Mustafar as the corrupted rebel [[3PO-series protocol droid|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]] and as the [[MSE-6 series repair droid|MSE-6 droid]] [[Petyr]] on a [[Taylander shuttle]].<ref name="Dark Droids 2">[[Dark Droids 2|''Dark Droids'' 2]]</ref> The initial [[Scourge attack on Fortress Vader|attack on Fortress Vader]] failed as the Scourge's attention was diverted by an [[Attack on Scourge 01|attack]] elsewhere and the breakthrough of being able to control the consciousness of cyborg organics.<ref name="Dark Droids 3">[[Dark Droids 3|''Dark Droids'' 3]]</ref>

While training with his droid army, Vader received a hologram transmission from Grand Vizier Amedda, who relayed the Emperor's order to reclaim his flagship, the ''[[Executor]]''—it had been [[Attack on the Executor (Scourge crisis)|infiltrated]] by the Scourge. Vader and his droids thus departed for the ''Executor'' aboard an [[Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial transport]].<ref name="DV202037" /> After successfully reclaiming the flagship, the Sith Lord took his droids and his personal [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced|TIE fighter]] and returned to Mustafar, where another droid repaired its fellow veterans while Vader confronted the Eye of Webbish Bog, demanding power and control—while battling the Scourge, Amedda had ordered the ''Executor''{{'s}} destruction with Vader onboard. The Eye reminded Vader that power lied with his master, Darth Sidious, citing the [[Tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise]] in which Sidious murdered his own master. While Vader prepared to depart for Coruscant's Imperial Palace with his droids and a ''Lambda''-class [[shuttle]], one of his droids, [[ZED-6-7]], succumbed to the Scourge and activated an [[octuptarra tri-droid]] in the secret Techno Union droid factory.<ref name="DV202038">[[Darth Vader (2020) 38|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 38]]</ref>

The octuptarra [[Attack on Vader|attacked]] Vader on the lava plains, and the Sith Lord's crude Force power through his Zaly Shield and staff proved ineffective. In their attempt to trigger Vader's hatred so that he could further draw on the dark power that hate channeled, the Dark Lord's droids [[G-90|Gee-Ninety]] and [[Arex]] joined in the attack, but to no avail. Arex urged the Sith to think about what he hated most, and the cyborg realized that he hated himself; using his self-loathing, Vader channeled his hate into fine Force power to destroy the Scourge's octuptarra, damaging Gee-Ninety, Arex, and ZED-6-7 in the process. Vader also found that he hated his master, Darth Sidious, even more than himself, and set off for Coruscant<ref name="DV202039">[[Darth Vader (2020) 39|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 39]]</ref> with a compliment of Scourge [[spider-droid]]s aboard his [[TIE Advanced x1]], setting the stage for a confrontation with his master and the [[Scourge of Coruscant]].<ref name="DV202040">[[Darth Vader (2020) 40|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 40]]</ref>

Vader's attack failed, as the Emperor turned Vader's own troops, including his hand-picked squad of death troopers, against him.<ref name="DV202040" /> Vader eliminated the squad and had their bodies sent to a medical lab on Mustafar. There the Sith Lord mused that although the death troopers organic minds made them superior to droids, it also supplied them with a will that could be turned against him.<ref name="Tool of the Empire">{{StoryCite|story=Tool of the Empire|book=Revelations (2023) 1}}</ref> Following the end of the droid crisis, Vader sought to appropriate the Scourge's ability to control automatons and cyborgs for his own ends. The Dark Lord captured the members of [[M.A.R. Corps]]—a Rebel Alliance squad of cybernetically-enhanced commandos—and brought them to Mustafar for experimentation. Under the supervision of ZED-6-7, the rebels were equipped with droid brains that allowed Vader to interface with and command them. The process was extremely invasive, however, causing severe mental anguish in the commandos that was shared by Vader. During these experiments, [[Administrator]] Sly Moore met with Vader in his fortress with the intent of persuading him to join her [[Schism Imperial]], a splinter group of disaffected Imperial officers and bureaucrats who planned to overthrow the Emperor.<ref name="DV202042">[[Darth Vader (2020) 42|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 42]]</ref>

Vader and the Schism's crusade against the Emperor finally came to a head in a [[Skirmish on Caranthanax B|skirmish]] on [[Caranthanax B]], where Vader fully submitted to the will of the Emperor. The aftermath of the battle saw the Schism revealed as a ruse concocted by Palpatine, as well the recovery of [[Energy capsule (technology)|energy capsules]] from the site by the former slaves [[Kitster Banai]] and [[Wald]]. Ochi of Bestoon later recovered the capsules on [[Tatooine]] and presented them to Vader in his castle throne room on Mustafar.<ref name="DV202050">[[Darth Vader (2020) 50|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 50]]</ref>

===Ashes of Empire (4–35 ABY)===
====Lingering darkness====
{{Quote|It is not over. Not yet. Not while you can bring him back…your master will ''return'' to the fires of Mustafar and, this time, will be made whole… Vader triumphant. Vader supreme. Vader… ''reborn''!|A voice speaks to Vaneé|<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />}}
Toward the end of the Galactic Civil War, Vader was saved by the selfless compassion of his son, Luke Skywalker, and in turn sacrificed himself to destroy the Emperor<ref name="Anakin DB">{{Databank|anakin-skywalker|Anakin Skywalker}}</ref> aboard the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]] during the Battle of [[Endor]] in 4 ABY.<ref name="Timelines" /> Having re-embraced his identity as Anakin Skywalker as he succumbed to the injuries [[Force lightning|inflicted]] upon him by his late Sith Master,<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Vader died leaving his fortress without a host.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> After the battle, [[New Republic pilot|pilot]] [[Wedge Antilles]] scouted suspected Imperial planets and reported his findings to the leadership of the [[New Republic]]—the Rebellion's successor state—on the world [[Raydonia]]; due to Mustafar's proximity to Raydonia, Admiral [[Gial Ackbar]] sent a scout to there, along with the planets Tatooine, [[Dermos]], [[Geonosis]], and [[Akiva]].<ref name="Aftermath" />

Following news of Darth Vader's death over Endor that the Rebel Alliance had broadcasted, Mustafarians gathered around the fortress' vicinity in celebration. Lightning storm clouds and lava on Mustafar stirred around Vader's castle, howls sounded in the night, and cries echoed across the lava plains. The Mustafarian boy [[Giggek]] recognized that his kind were not truly free as long as they lived under the shadow of Vader's castle, and so resolved to rid the land of Vader's curse by bringing the castle to ruin. Along with [[Tuttel]], Giggek acquired [[Bomb|detonators]] from a store of equipment from the obsidian mines belonging to Tuttel's uncle, Lellis. However, the latter forbid the young boys from entering Vader's castle for the reason that it was lethal and evil, telling the story of how Vaneé came into servitude under Vader and further speculating that the young Mustafarians were only pursuing glory.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

[[File:LellisWarnsGiggek-ShadowOfVadersCastle.jpg|thumb|left|360px|Two young Mustafarians ventured into Fortress Vader despite being cautioned against doing so by Lellis.]]
Nevertheless, Giggek led Tuttel into Vader's castle by way of lava flea, venturing in to find a pit trapping Vaneé, the servant of Vader and the self-styled "one true [[Acolytes of the Beyond|Acolyte of the Beyond]]" who was detained by Vader there some time ago. Rescuing the Acolyte in hopes of not bringing death upon anyone in the process of destroying Vader's castle, Giggek was at once betrayed by Vaneé, who dropped the boy down the pit in hopes of bringing death to those who sought to tarnish his master's legacy. However, after instructing his Mustafarian companion to flee, which Tuttel did with their lava flea, Giggek ignited his explosives through a remote [[detonator]], and although the blast did not bring down Vader's castle, Vaneé was buried in black sand. However, the Sith servant survived. A voice familiar to Vaneé told him not to fear, and assured its servant that he could return Vader to the fires of Mustafar and be made whole.<ref name="Shadow of Vader" />

====Wrath of Vader's ghost====
{{Quote|And I'm sorry. You of all people must be—''"<br />"''Scared out of my wits? Wishing I'd never even heard the ''word'' Mustafar? It's the dreams, Lina. They're getting to us all.''"<br />"''You're right, Hudd. That's all they are… dreams. And dreams aren't real… Dreams can't hurt you.|Lina Graf and Thom Hudd, on Mustafar once more|<ref name="Ghosts 4">[[Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle 4|''Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle'' 4]]</ref>}}
At some point, Vaneé witnessed holonews reports on the Battle of Endor and the death of Vader, but he refused to believe that his master had met his end. The acolyte continued to maintain the Dark Lord's castle, anticipating his return at any time.<ref name="Legacy of Vaneé">{{StoryCite|story=Legacy of Vaneé|book=Free Comic Book Day 2025: Star Wars 1|bformatted=Free Comic Book Day 2025: ''Star Wars'' 1}}</ref> Following the Empire's defeat at<ref name="Ghosts 1">[[Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle 1|''Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle'' 1]]</ref> the [[Battle of Jakku]] in [[5 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Vaneé told the voice he believed to be his master that everyone in the galaxy believed that he was dead, which the supposed ghost of Vader replied to by saying that the Sith can never truly be killed since it was the will of the dark side. Vaneé then orchestrated a ritual in which Vader's ghost reached out across the galaxy to imprint nightmares upon others' minds. One such nightmare reached [[Milo Graf]], brother of Lina Graf, in which Milo had a nightmare about undead droids and himself being taken to Mustafar by [[CR-8R]], controlled by Vaneé.<ref name="Ghosts 1" />

After he discussed Vader's castle with his sister and CR-8R, Milo Graf and the droid went missing for days<ref name="Ghosts 2">[[Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle 2|''Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle'' 2]]</ref>—CR-8R had been afflicted by a signal that scrambled his processors<ref name="Ghosts 5">[[Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle 5|''Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle'' 5]]</ref> and had incapacitated the organic before bringing him to Vaneé on Mustafar. Suffering from a dream of her brother being trapped on Mustafar, Lina requested New Republic [[Chancellor (New Republic)|Chancellor]] Mon Mothma and Senator [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] on the capital world [[Chandrila]] to spare a ship to investigate the lava world, which had remained under Imperial control. Although Mothma denied Graf's request, Organa suggested that she contact the smuggler [[Jaxxon T. Tumperakki]] for passage to Mustafar.<ref name="Ghosts 2" /> Before arriving at Vader's castle, they enlisted Graf's old crew, Thom Hudd and [[Skritt]]; Hudd had also been experiencing nightmares related to Vaneé and the fortress.<ref name="Ghosts 3">[[Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle 3|''Star Wars Adventures: Ghosts of Vader's Castle'' 3]]</ref>

En route to Mustafar aboard the ''[[Rabbit's Foot]]'', Lina Graf experienced a nightmare where her crew was attacked by an Imperial [[Gozanti-class Assault Carrier|''Gozanti''-class cruiser]] and TIE fighters upon arriving in the Mustafar system. Mid-battle, Lina Graf was attacked by the phantom of Darth Vader and encountered her brother, Milo, who transformed into Darth Vader and killed her crewmates. When Lina awoke from her nightmare, her crew and their ship had landed at Fortress Vader.<ref name="Ghosts 4" /> While the crew broke into the installation, Lina was contacted by Milo via comlink, pleading to be rescued. They then encountered a machine resembling Darth Vader and wielding a blue-bladed lightsaber, but promptly destroyed it and found CR-8R, who regained his normal processing and revealed Vaneé to be the mastermind.<ref name="Ghosts 5" />

[[File:AnakinGhost-GhostsOfVadersCastle5.png|thumb|right|230px|Anakin Skywalker as a Force spirit, having rescued the crew of Lina Graf from the ghosts of Vader's castle]]
Vaneé soon captured the crew, intending to use them for a ritual that supposedly would revive Darth Vader. He released lava fumes into the captivity chamber, declaring that Lina Graf would be the vessel for Vader's return and that the Dark Lord would be immortal, ushering a new empire. However, Lina saw through Vaneé's madness and the hallucinations brought by the lava fumes, conquering her fear; taking advantage of Vaneé's fear for Vader, she deceived the man and freed her crew with the blue lightsaber. Upon forcing Vaneé into the restraints that he had used to detain her, Lina fled just as her blade extinguished, leaving Vaneé trapped with his own nightmares within the castle. Before departing Mustafar safely, however, Lina's crew followed the light of a blue blade in order to flee Fortress Vader—unbeknownst to them, the light was created by the [[Force spirit]] of Anakin Skywalker, Jedi Knight.<ref name="Ghosts 5" />

====A healing world====
{{Quote|Black Sun is currently headquartered on the lava planet Mustafar and is mainly controlled by Vigos from several noble Falleen families.|"Index of Organizations"|<ref name="Species From A to Z">{{GermanFanCite|115|Database|Species From A to Z}}</ref>}}
[[File:VadersCastleBattlefield-SWH.png|300px|thumb|left|A recreation of Vader's Castle, used as an arena on Vespaara]]
Mustafar grew in obscurity in the decades that followed, and Vader's castle eventually fell into ruins.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Thanks to the destruction of the Bright Star,<ref name="Immortal 3" /> Mustafar's ecosystem began to be healed.<ref name="TROS VD" /> In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Hunters Date">{{HuntersDate}}</ref> the competitive sporting show [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]] featured many environments for its [[Hunter (Grand Arena)|cast]] to contend in, including [[Vader's Castle]]—a battlefield that was modeled after Fortress Vader and Mustafar's scorching surface—at the [[Grand Arena]] on the planet [[Vespaara]]. To complete the immersion of the battlefield, a wide screen projection was used at the side to display Mustafar's rocky terrain and flowing lava rivers.<ref name="SWH">''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''</ref> One Hunter, the former stormtrooper [[Sentinel]], utilized a pro-Imperial persona on the show and exaggerated his exploits as a soldier, though in truth he had grown to hate the Empire.<ref name="Battle for the Arena">''[[Hunters: Battle for the Arena]]''</ref> He claimed to have been deployed to a very hot lava planet and fought against a [[Fireworm]] on that world, although he could not recall if it had been Mustafar or [[Senna]].<ref name="Sentinel M2">{{HuntersCite|quest=Sentinel Mastery II}}</ref> In another instance, Sentinel claimed he once went to Mustafar as part of a [[pilgrim]]age, but was called away before he could complete his journey to the remains of Fortress Vader.<ref name="Crimson Vanguard">{{HuntersCite|character=Sentinel|costume=Crimson Vanguard}}</ref> Another Hunter, the [[Ugnaught]] [[Dizzy (Ugnaught)|Dizzy]], used bronzium acquired from Mustafarian mines to maintain a [[Team Slingshot droideka|droideka]] that served as his partner in the arena.<ref name="Prospect Paintwork" />

Around the same year,<ref name="Skeleton Crew Date">{{SkeletonCrewDate}}</ref> the [[astronomer]] [[Kh'ymm]] attempted to uncover the coordinates to the long-lost planet [[At Attin]] from her [[Unidentified telescopic array|facility]] on the [[Observatory Moon]]. Mustafar was one of the many worlds in her database that she scoured through to find the legendary planet.<ref name="Astrogation Problem">{{SkeletonCrew|Very Interesting, As an Astrogation Problem}}</ref> A variety of individuals from off-world visited the planet during this period,<ref name="TROS VD" /> including the spy [[Vi Moradi]]<ref name="Return to a Shattered Planet">{{StoryCite|story=Black Spire: Return to a Shattered Planet|book=Galaxy's Edge: Black Spire}}</ref> as well as the [[historian]] and adventurer [[Eloc Throno]], who wrote of the world in ''[[Volcanic Planets: Your Guide to the Galaxy's Hottest Destinations]]'', one of the many travel guides he wrote throughout his career.<ref name="Travel Guide to Batuu">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]''</ref> By the [[New Republic Era]], Black Sun had resumed operations on Mustafar, which served as its headquarters. During this time, Mustafar was also mentioned in "[[Index of Organizations]]," a survival compendium sent out by [[Carson Teva]], which mentioned Black Sun's operations as well as the rescue of Marg Krim's family during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Species From A to Z" />

By [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Legacy of Vader Date">[[Legacy of Vader 1|''Legacy of Vader'' 1]] takes place directly after the events of {{Film|VIII}}, which occur in [[34 ABY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''.</ref> many pilgrims had come to the ruins of Vader's castle seeking to tap into the Sith Lord's dark power. One group of pilgrims,<ref name="TROS VD" /> the [[Alazmec of Winsit]], guarded the castle ruins as well as its secrets jealously,<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> colonizing the nearby Corvax Fen and planting a forest of irontrees in the hopes of restoring Mustafar's once lush landscape from centuries ago, believing that the soil was soaked by the tears of Lady Corvax.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The [[Sith cultist|cultists]] cared for the trees as they sought to connect to the power of the Sith.<ref name="CEUEE">''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> The Alazmec also venerated Vader's memory and defended Mustafar's secrets against seekers whom they considered unworthy.<ref name="Alazmec DB">{{Databank|alazmec|Alazmec}}</ref> Vader's aging advisor Vaneé lived amongst them at the Dark Lord's castle;<ref name="Legacy of Vader 1">[[Legacy of Vader 1|''Legacy of Vader'' 1]]</ref> though ancient by human standards, he had extended his lifespan through extreme cybernetic augmentations not unlike those once undergone by Vader himself. Although he continued to tend to the castle grounds, he eventually came to acknowledge that Darth Vader had truly died and would never again haunt the cooling plains of Mustafar.<ref name="Legacy of Vaneé" />

====Dark prince's homecoming====
{{Quote|Darth Vader is the past. This entire ''place'' is the past. The past ''strangles'' me. Its expectations and legacies and vendettas. I will destroy every last vestige of it. I will ''free myself''.|Kylo Ren, in the halls of Vader's castle|<ref name="Legacy of Vader 1" />}}
[[File:Steadfast-Mustafar-TROS.png|thumb|left|360px|Mustafar was visited multiple times by Kylo Ren, Supreme Leader of the First Order, years after the death of his grandfather, Darth Vader.]]
After the [[First Order]] nearly destroyed the [[Resistance]] at the [[Battle of Crait]]<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> in 34 ABY,<ref name="Legacy of Vader Date" /> the faction's newly ascended [[Supreme Leader]] [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]] sought to rid himself of all connections to his past, including his maternal grandfather, Darth Vader.<ref name="Legacy of Vader 1" /> Knowing that Vader once ruled Mustafar, Ren had at a time regarded it as hallowed ground—the place where Anakin Skywalker died and a Dark Lord of the Sith was born.<ref name="TROS JN" /> He traveled to Mustafar alone aboard [[Kylo Ren's TIE silencer|his TIE silencer]] with the intent of destroying the legacy of Vader that remained on the planet. On this personal crusade, he encountered members of the Alazmec of Winsit<ref name="Legacy of Vader 1" />—who deemed Ren unworthy of Mustafar's secrets<ref name="Alazmec DB" />—and slew them at the entrance of his grandfather's fortress. Inside he met Vaneé, who convinced Ren that his past could be used as a weapon, as even Vader had used his painful memories to deepen his connection to the dark side. The two departed Mustafar and traveled to Tatooine to uncover more of Ren's [[Skywalker family|family history]].<ref name="Legacy of Vader 1" />

Failing to find the power he sought elsewhere in the galaxy, a frustrated Ren returned to Vader's Castle to find a means of summoning the spirit of Luke Skywalker for a final reckoning. Ren used his grandfather's [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber|meditation chamber]] to clear his mind at Vaneé's instruction. Although he was seemingly able to commune with Skywalker through a [[Force vision]], he also encountered dark reflections of figures from his past that left him physically wounded.<ref name="Legacy of Vader 10">[[Legacy of Vader 10|''Legacy of Vader'' 10]]</ref> With the Supreme Leader in a weakened state, Vaneé saw an opportunity to fulfill his ultimate goal: the birth of a new Vader. The cyborg adorned Ren with Vader's helmet and restrained him in an apparatus that was meant to lower him into the fires and fumes of Mustafar, but Ren escaped and pursued the old man through the booby-trapped fortress.<ref name="Legacy of Vader 11">[[Legacy of Vader 11|''Legacy of Vader'' 11]]</ref>

Ren destroyed four [[DT-series sentry droid]]s that stood against him before finally confronting Vaneé at the entrance of a [[Darth Vader's vault|vault]] that the Sith acolyte had once claimed to be the storehouse of Vader's power. Tired of his tricks, Ren pushed Vaneé through the observation window of the castle and sent him plummeting into the lava below, ending the unnaturally long life of Vader's most devout servant. With only his desire for power remaining, Ren entered the vault.<ref name="Legacy of Vader 11" /> Inside, he encountered a vision of himself, first donned in the armor of his grandfather, then draped in the [[Jedi apparel|robes of a Jedi Knight]]. The apparition encouraged Ren to seek his own truth and move forward before sending him hurtling out of the castle.<ref name="Legacy of Vader 12">[[Legacy of Vader 12|''Legacy of Vader'' 12]]</ref>

Around the same time, the [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] wrote about Mustafar in his [[book]] ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]''.<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Elsewhere, the confused [[Resistance pilot|pilot]] [[Shriv Suurgav]] uttered "what in the depths of Mustafar?" during his [[Mission to Bracca|mission]] to acquire starfighters for the Resistance when [[First Order stormtrooper|First Order stormtroopers]] he was fighting began to be hit by [[arrow]]s from the [[Bracca resistance]].<ref name="Resistance Reborn">''[[Resistance Reborn]]''</ref>

====Pathway to the Sith Eternal====
{{Quote|I must warn you, our fiery planet burns away deception. If you proceed down this path, you will encounter your true self.|Eye of Webbish Bog, to Kylo Ren|<ref name="TROS EE">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]''</ref>}}
In 35 ABY,<ref name="Timelines" /> the First Order [[Resurgent-class Star Destroyer|''Resurgent''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Steadfast (Resurgent-class)|''Steadfast'']] arrived over Mustafar following a mysterious [[Exegol Broadcast|broadcast]] from the resurrected Darth Sidious.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Supreme Leader Ren had again returned to the world once ruled by his grandfather, this time accompanied by the might of the [[First Order Navy]]. Landing in his [[TIE/wi modified interceptor|TIE whisper]] with General [[Armitage Hux]] and [[Allegiant General]] [[Enric Pryde]] observing him from afar,<ref name="TROS EE" /> Kylo Ren rallied his forces to Mustafar as part of his [[Search for Exegol|search for answers]] to confront whoever was behind the transmission. The Supreme Leader and his stormtroopers [[Mission to Mustafar (First Order)|slaughtered]] what remained of the [[Religion|cult]] of Alazmec colonists near the ruins of Vader's castle,<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref> who were sworn to protect the surrounding fen.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Afterward, Ren traveled through the fen and arrived at a small lake, where he encountered the Eye of Webbish Bog.<ref name="TROS EE" />

[[File:Kylo_Mustafar.png|thumb|right|320px|Ren killed the Alazmec colonists before claiming the Sith wayfinder that once belonged to his grandfather.]]
The Eye knew what Ren sought but warned him of encountering his "true self" if he were to continue down his current path. When Ren did not respond, the Eye relented and rewarded the Supreme Leader for his victory over the Alazmec, pointing the way to Vader's Sith wayfinder.<ref name="TROS EE" /> Ren was guided by wisps of the dark side and came to an altar surrounded by the fortress ruins where he found the wayfinder.<ref name="TROS JN" /> The Eye of Webbish Bog then disappeared into the lake, leaving Ren alone with the artifact. Knowing that he would not be the only one to travel to Mustafar in search of the object,<ref name="TROS EE" /> Ren, with the word "Exegol" suddenly in his thoughts,<ref name="TROS VD" /> departed the planet with the rest of the First Order forces. The Eye's prophecy soon came true: Ren reached the planet Exegol, where he found the resurrected Sidious with his [[Sith Eternal]] followers, and eventually [[Mission to Kef Bir|returned]] to abiding by the light side of the Force, joining the Jedi [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] to [[Battle of Exegol|destroy]] Sidious once and for all, ending the [[First Order-Resistance War|galactic war]].<ref name="TROS EE" />

After the destruction of Sidious at the Battle of Exegol, the [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] penned the [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''. In the book, Kin wrote about Mustafar's feared reputation and referenced the file titled "Mustafar" in the [[Imperial Archives]] section about Darth Vader.<ref name="Rise and Fall">''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
===The Mustafarians===
{{Quote|Mustafar is our world. We have already lost so much. The lifefires barely burn. It is time to come together…and save what is left.|Father Kkkt|<ref name="DV23" />}}
[[File:KkktAttacksFortressVader-2017DarthVader23.png|thumb|left|350px|However harsh and volcanic, Mustafar was not devoid of life.]]
Boasting a population of approximately 15,000<ref name="TROS VD" /> to 20,000 individuals,<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Mustafar was the [[homeworld]] of the Mustafarians, a species primarily concerned with their own advancement and survival<ref name="SM" /> that lived in underground caves created by the lava fleas that ate through the planet's crust.<ref name="AEYNK" /> Two races of Mustafarians evolved in distinctly different cave systems<ref name="TROS VD" /> in the mountains from extremophile arthropods,<ref name="CL" /> [[Southern Mustafarian|one subspecies]] living near the planet's equator and the [[Northern Mustafarian|other]] in the north. They lived together as needed, although the geographical distance and limited desirable living space tended to limit the subspecies in their own communities.<ref name="SM" />

Only venturing up to the surface in order to collect valuable minerals from the lava flows, the southern Mustafarians carried out the heavy labor involved due to<ref name="AEYNK" /> their short and strong physiology that developed due to the relatively higher gravity of their homeland, surviving high temperatures and frequent accidents on lava flows thanks to their thick carapaces, while the tall and slender northern Mustafarians had keen, faceted [[eye]]s which easily spotted flaws in ore and machinery alike,<ref name="SM" /> and who acted as guards and expert riders of the lava flea, a creature that the natives made their armor from the heat-resistant shells of.<ref name="AEYNK" />

Chitinous exoskeletons and low-[[water]] biology allowed Mustafarians to withstand the intense heat of their homeworld, although they still required insulated clothes and breathing apparatus to work on the surface.<ref name="CL" /> The native Mustafarians developed and sought technology for survival more so than most other species, and some enhanced themselves with cybernetics to better carry out common tasks and withstand the harsh environments of their homeworld. Having learned from tragic experiences, Mustafarians did not trust imported technology until they themselves modified and adapted them to Mustafar's climes. While the two Mustafarian subspecies lived together as needed, the geographical distance and limited desirable living space tended to keep them in their own communities,<ref name="SM" /> although it was not unheard of for clans to be comprised of both northern and southern Mustafarians.<ref name="DV21" />

[[File:Mustafarian_lava_buns.jpg|thumb|right|224px|Mustafar's volcanic crust allowed for the creation of Mustafarian Lava Buns.]]
The Mustafarians grew few crops, as the lack of water meant traditional [[farm]]s, even when located underground, could not be sustained;<ref name="SM" /> water had to be imported to Mustafar.<ref name="AEYNK" /> Nevertheless, despite the what little life Mustafar had compared to other worlds, various types of edible fungi and domesticated herds of large insectoid creatures made up much of the Mustafarian diet, and unlike other hotbeds of industry in the galaxy, Mustafar was largely self-sufficient in regards to its food supply.<ref name="SM" />

Southern Mustafarians made [[Mustafarian Lava Bun]]s by placing sweet balls of dough upon the planet's volcanic crust, heating it up to create a red bread with a cracked and blackened exterior. The [[Artiodac]] [[chef]] [[Strono Tuggs]] witnessed the production of the baked goods during a visit to Mustafar, learning the recipe to the buns in the process. Tuggs later served the buns at his mobile [[Tuggs' Grub|restaurant]] on the Outer Rim planet [[Batuu]] after the [[Battle of Takodana|fall]] of his previous [[Takodana Castle|place]] of employment on [[Takodana]]<ref name="BSOC">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: The Official Black Spire Outpost Cookbook]]''</ref> in 34 ABY.<ref name="Timelines" />

Although they typically inhabited natural caverns and abandoned mines, Mustafarians built outdoor structures as necessary, including saucer-shaped buildings at and near active mining sites. Their structures were strongly reinforced and armored to protect them from natural disasters, making their larger facilities [[fortress]]like in construction and durability.<ref name="SM" />

The Mustafarian people shared a deep connection with their planet,<ref name="DV21" /> seeking harmony with the natural forces that sculpted their homeworld.<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Surrounded by volcanic magma, their culture was tied to the ebbs and flows of the lava on which they lived.<ref name="DV21" /> In the difficult times of the Empire, history and lore of Mustafar lived on in a Mustafarian leader known as the Priestess, who provided guidance and invaluable information to natives and visitors alike.<ref name="Priestess DB">{{Databank|priestess|Priestess}}</ref> The natives lived in clans,<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> and members of Father Kkkt's clan spoke of "lifefires" and "endfires" while discussing the arrival of Darth Vader; Kkkt himself used the Force to form a symbol within a lava river, which he interpreted as an omen of the planet's future. The Mustafarians had a strong desire to protect their homeworld, banding together<ref name="DV21" /> on multiple occasions to defend against Imperial forces.<ref name="Tales 5" /> They had a special relationship with the other life on Mustafar; lava fleas were used to jump over lava flows in a rite of passage, and kahel cave fungi served as the inspiration for Mustafarian architecture.<ref name="CL" /> The Priestess spoke of a being known as [[Sleeper]], whom she prayed to after encountering a deceased darkghast.<ref name="Immortal 2" />

[[File:MustafariansSwarmFortress-TalesFromVadersCastle5.png|thumb|left|350px|The Mustafarians were fierce defenders of their planet.]]
Mustafarians were politically organized in accordance with the caverns and communities they inhabited, although they had little in the way of a central government. However, some trusted leaders were allowed to make deals with offworlders in order to help ensure their survival and quality of life. As a result, the Mustafarians fell under the sway of the Techno Union and later the Mining Guild,<ref name="SM" /> serving them as ore scouts, miners, and refinery laborers. While they resented the presence of offworlders,<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Mustafarians were generally willing to tolerate a degree of outside political influence as long as it furthered their own cause. Because of the demanding environment of their world, Mustafarians were generally insular and disinterested in galactic affairs, few regarding offworlders with much curiosity. Their focus on the advancement and survival of their own species overrode other concerns, a result of inhabiting a world that demanded so much in order to so much as continue living.<ref name="SM" />

Mustafarians spoke a [[language]] of the [[Mustafarian (language)|same name]],<ref name="Tales 5" /> which allowed for the precise expression of concepts related to naturals features above and below ground, especially phenomena that were deceptively dangerous. Although the Mustafarian subspecies spoke different dialects, any two individuals could communicate on a functional level despite differing terms and cultural concepts. While they were also capable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard|Basic]] and other common galactic languages, most that did not work with the Mining Guild or deal with outsiders by necessity did not bother to learn Basic. However, Mustafarians that lived or traveled offworld almost always spoke Basic and sometimes the language of their trading partners. Due to their history with the Techno Union, they were more likely to know languages regularly used among former Separatist worlds.<ref name="SM" />

Mustafarian travels off-world were driven by business pursuits and trade negotiations, and were generally restricted to the Outer Rim. So long as their safety or that of their companions was not threatened, the species was disinterested in galactic affairs, which made them foremost disinclined to leave their homeworld. For Mustafarian merchants and Mining Guild personnel, regular trips were made off-world to trade for upgrades in protective technology and equipment, as well as to deliver ores to buyers. However, there were some Mustafarians who sought full-time employment off-world. They found most inhabited worlds cold, yet relished the relative safety.<ref name="SM" />

===Invaders and colonizers===
====Before the Empire====
[[File:BlackSunLeaders-Eminence.png|thumb|right|333px|Black Sun's Falleen leadership was based out of Mustafar until the Empire established a garrison on the planet.]]
The Techno Union, a guild of technology firms led by [[Skakoan]]s like [[Wat Tambor]],<ref name="Techno Union DB">{{Databank|techno-union|Techno Union}}</ref> came to value the lucrative minerals of Mustafar and set up operations on the planet.<ref name="CL" /> The offworlders introduced heavy industry, and were welcomed by the native Mustafarians in exchange for access to mining droids and heavy-duty speeders.<ref name="SM" /> However, the natives became subjugated, being put to work in the Techno Union's mining operations<ref name="CL" /> and charged rent on their own planet.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Management staff of the Union utilized native buildings throughout their operations and provided a refuge for the Separatist Council during the final days of the Clone Wars.<ref name="CL" /> Mining droids used on Mustafar<ref name="ROTS" /> during its time under Techno Union ownership<ref name="CVD" /> included the ore extraction droid, the DLC-13 mining droid, and the electrorefining droid. A number of Separatist battle droids and mouse droids were also present within the facility used by the Separatist Council in the late Clone Wars.<ref name="ROTS" />

Aside from the native people and the Techno Union, Mustafar was also inhabited by Falleen,<ref name="Eminence" /> tall and muscular [[reptomammal]]ians native<ref name="HC17">{{HelmetCollectionCite|17|Databank A-Z}}</ref> to the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TFABG" /> planet of the [[Falleen (planet)|same name]]<ref name="HC17" /> that controlled the vast Black Sun criminal empire. [[Humanoid]]s with distinctly [[Alien|nonhuman]] appearances, they had ridged [[Skeleton|skulls]],<ref name="Falleen">{{Databank|falleen|Falleen}}</ref> scaly green skin,<ref name="HC17" /> and exuded powerful [[pheromone]]s to attract mates.<ref name="Dark Disciple" />

====Vader's sanctum====
{{Quote|We bow only to one, the Dark Lord, the true father and ruler of the galaxy. Vader.|Kylo Ren's translation of an Alazmec warning|<ref name="TROS JN" />}}
The Sith Lord Darth Vader called Mustafar his home during the Imperial Era. Originally coming to the planet in hopes of resurrecting his deceased wife,<ref name="DV21" /> Vader lived on the volcanic world for over a decade, utilizing its scorched earth to conduct his personal business,<ref name="Rogue One" /> and ruled the entire star system<ref name="Kenobi IV" /> from his castle and its [[Vader's throne room|throne room]].<ref name="Kenobi III" /> Stories of the Jedi who died by his hand on Mustafar became synonymous with the planet itself.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> During his visit to Fortress Vader, Director Krennic theorized that Mustafar was Vader's homeworld, imagining that the Dark Lord's cybernetics were designed to allow him to survive while away from the molten planet.<ref name="Rogue One novel" /> The Sith Lord's occupancy was known to others in the galaxy as well. After discovering that Mustafar was Vader's domain, the [[Naboo (people)|Naboo]] resistance group known as the Amidalans deduced that he was responsible for Padmé's death and plotted to kill the Dark Lord to avenge the fallen [[Monarch of Naboo|queen]].<ref name="Vader 2020 3">[[Darth Vader (2020) 3|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 3]]</ref>

[[File:Dv22Gist.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Vader became the dark lord of Mustafar from his obsidian fortress.]]
As Darth Vader established his personal headquarters on Mustafar, the forces of the Galactic Empire followed.<ref name="DV21" /> Vaneé entered Vader's service as custodian of his castle<ref name="Shadow of Vader" /> in 12 BBY,<ref name="Timelines" /> tending to the Sith Lord's daily needs,<ref name="Legacy of Vaneé" /> while Admiral Karius served as Vader's second-in-command on the planet<ref name="Karius" /> by 1 BBY.<ref name="Timelines" /> The Imperials' occupation of the planet forced Black Sun<ref name="TROS VD" /> and the Techno Union to abandon their operations, with the Mining Guild taking over what remained.<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> Within both Vader's fortress<ref name="Tales 5" /> as well as other installations, the [[Imperial Army]] had a sizable presence on the world,<ref name="Secrets" /> enough that the native population sought to remove them from the planet.<ref name="Return 5" /> Stormtroopers guarded Imperial interests on Mustafar;<ref name="Secrets" /> among their ranks were [[magma trooper]]s<ref name="DV23" /> and Lava Troopers, specialized soldiers that operated within the planet's volcanic environment.<ref name="Tales 5" /> M.A.R. Corps of the Rebel Alliance was briefly stationed on Mustafar after being forcibly conscripted by Darth Vader.<ref name="DV202042" />

Many groups of cultists came to Mustafar in the decades since Vader's passing, seeking the power that the Sith Lord once tapped into on the planet. One of those groups, called the Alazmec of Winsit, gained control of Corvax Fen. They planted several irontrees in its fertile soils in the hopes of restoring the landscape that was once present centuries ago, and were devoted to guarding it from outsiders such as Kylo Ren and the First Order.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Formed from members of the [[Alazmec]] species, the group wore [[Night-vision goggles|night-vision lenses]] and weather-resistant [[poncho]]s.<ref name="CEUEE" />

===Other inhabitants===
{{Quote|Lady Corvax abided here with her husband Sir Dorwin, living in peace with my people.|The Priestess speaks to the descendant of Lady Corvax|<ref name="Immortal 1" />}}
[[File:Lady_Corvax.png|thumb|right|220px|Lady Corvax was responsible for Mustafar's devastation.]]
In the planet's vibrant past, the Mustafarians shared the world with Lady Corvax and her husband Dorwin, humanoids who lived peacefully with the natives. Dorwin fell in battle,<ref name="Immortal 1" /> but he did not die; instead, he was cursed to exist between life and death on the ruined world<ref name="Immortal 2" /> until he was freed by Corvax's descendant.<ref name="Immortal 3" />

The ancient Sith established a presence on Mustafar, hoping to reap the benefits of the dark world and obtain immortality.<ref name="TROS VD" /> At some point, the Sith Lord Momin found himself on Mustafar, and later, during the Imperial Era, recalled that long ago time.<ref name="DV22" />

Two mysterious beings resided in a lava cavern near Fortress Vader<ref name="Vader 2020 8" />—the [[spider]]-like Eye of Webbish Bog atop a [[Unidentified blind Arobernos|blind giant]], who were submerged in their lair and were locked in a symbiotic relationship. Their lair became a small lake beside the Corvax Fen, and they guarded the path to the ruins of Vader's castle.<ref name="TROS EE" /> Spoken of in the myths of the Mustafarians, the Eye was defended by the Alazmec of Winsit.<ref name="TROS JN" />

==Locations==
{{Expandsect}}
===Settlements===
{{Dialogue|Vos|Where can we get a drink?|Mustafarian|The Last Resort.|Ventress|That the best bar in town?|Mustafarian|<nowiki />''Only'' bar in town.|attr=Quinlan Vos and Asajj Ventress ask a local for directions in Zitontown|src=<ref name="Dark Disciple" />}}
The native Mustafarian populace, including both the Northern and Southern sub-species, took up residence in underground caves that were made by lava fleas munching through Mustafar's crust.<ref name="AEYNK" /> Despite this, the two peoples lived in distinct underground cave systems, which resulted in their evolution into two sub-species.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The Mustafarians' underground buildings were designed in the shape of kahel cave fungus,<ref name="AEYNK" /> which was highly symbolic in Mustafarian culture.<ref name="CL" />

[[File:Complex.jpg|thumb|left|280px|A mining complex dots the molten surface of Mustafar.]]
Due to the planet's fiery surface, outdoor structures were built where necessary—usually at and near active mining sites<ref name="SM" />—and buildings on Mustafar were held up by stem-like gravity supports.<ref name="AEYNK" /> Its capital [[city]] was [[Fralideja]], one of the few remaining Mustafarian settlements at the time of the Clone Wars. A cataclysmic eruption that occurred centuries before the war's end almost destroyed the entire local population. The city and its surrounding structures were of Mustafarian architecture: mushroom-like structures with a habitation dome raised from the scorched ground, based on the shape of the local culture's highly symbolic kahel cave fungus.<ref name="CL" /> The saucer-shaped structures were strongly reinforced and armored against natural calamities, with larger facilities on Mustafar becoming fortresslike in construction and durability.<ref name="SM" /> Although Fralideja and its surrounding buildings that numbered several appeared modular, the structures varied in size and elevation.<ref name="CL" />

Another settlement was a mining town<ref name="Dark Disciple" /> known as Zitontown,<ref name="Galactic Explorer's Guide" /> named for Ziton Moj, a senior Black Sun [[Vigo]] who rose to leadership of the organization during the Clone Wars.<ref name="HC39">{{HelmetCollectionCite|39|Databank A-Z}}</ref> Located outside of town was a fortified<ref name="Dark Disciple" /> cliffside facility<ref name="Episode Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/eminence-episode-gallery|text="Eminence" Episode Gallery}} {{C|Slide 9}}</ref> that served as the organization's headquarters during the conflict.<ref name="BS DB" /> The installation's architecture was distinct from other facilities located on Mustafar.<ref name="Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/eminence-trivia-gallery|text="Eminence" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 5}}</ref> Miners from a variety of species lived and worked in Zitontown, most of whom were poorly nourished in comparison to the Falleen that inhabited the Black Sun fortress. In addition to the fortress, Moj also possessed a palace.<ref name="Dark Disciple" />

===Structures and installations===
{{Quote|Few people have the honor of seeing Lord Vader in his sanctum. I suggest you keep all you witnessed to yourself.|Vaneé, to Orson Krennic, upon the latter's arrival at Fortress Vader|<ref name="Rogue One novel" />}}
[[File:FortressVader-RogueOneWidevision-SWCT.png|thumb|right|280px|Darth Vader's Fortress on Mustafar]]
During the Clone Wars, Darth Sidious secretly maintained an old mining outpost on Mustafar, planning to use the facility to train Force-sensitive children to become his agents. The Sith tasked the bounty hunter Cad Bane with kidnapping children and delivering them to the facility for their training. However, it was destroyed by Sidious' crew of nanny droids after Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano rescued multiple kidnapped children from the facility.<ref name="Children of the Force" />

Mustafar was famous for its [[metal mine]]s,<ref name="Journey Through Space (2015)">[[Star Wars: Journey Through Space (2015)|''Star Wars: Journey Through Space'']]</ref> and was typically used by [[spacer]]s to refuel their vessels.<ref name="Children of the Force" /> The Techno Union maintained multiple mining operations on Mustafar, including a complex built into a lava-filled mountain—which also housed a secret battle droid factory—and a nearby residence for [[technician]]s and mine management staff located opposite to the capital city Fralideja. Around the area was a molten rock plain with erupting lava geysers that were repressed by the facility's repulsor fields. In addition to containing a secret command facility, the structure served as cover for a Techno Union droid [[Factory|production operation]] concealed inside the mountain upon which the mine sat, manufacturing battle droids<ref name="CL" /> for the Separatist Droid Army.<ref name="SM" /> The repulsor fields that protected the complex were inadvertently deactivated during the duel between Obi-Wan Kenobi and Darth Vader and the facility soon fell into ruin.<ref name="CL" />

[[File:Mustafar-ImpGarrison.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Fortress Vader and an Imperial base]]
Fortress Vader was an obsidian tower built by Lord Momin and Darth Vader as the latter's personal retreat on the Gahenn Plains during the Imperial Era.<ref name="Vader's castle DB">{{Databank|vader-s-castle|Vader's castle}}</ref> With a gap dividing the central body of the tower in the middle that resembled tuning forks, the fortress harnessed the surrounding lava for energy. It was also designed to channel the dark side's power,<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> and, along with being near the site of the Sith Lord's duel against his former master Obi-Wan Kenobi,<ref name="Vader's castle DB" /> it was located above an ancient Sith cave to provide a more powerful locus of the dark side for Darth Vader to draw upon.<ref name="Mustafar DB" /> It was also on the site of the underground fortress of Lady Corvax.<ref name="Immortal 1" /> When visiting the fortress, Imperial officers were intimidated by the surrounding environments, and the treacherous landscape of Mustafar worked to remind them of their place.<ref name="USWNE" /> Vader's castle had an Imperial base in its vicinity, which housed a part of the garrison protecting Vader's sanctum.<ref name="Secrets" />

===Other landmarks===
{{Quote|Mustafar is not like other planets. It is ''unique''. Deep beneath its surface rests a locus for the ''dark side'' of the Force.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Vader|<ref name="DV5" />}}
[[File:SithCave-2017DarthVader5.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Sith cave housed a powerful heart of darkness.]]
Formerly a part of a Sith temple, the cave beneath Vader's castle contained a locus of the dark side of the Force.<ref name="USWNE" /> The walls of the cave were covered in glowing runic symbols, which Vader and Momin later rearranged to focus the energies of the planet. By tapping into the dark powers of the locus, an individual could open a rift between time and space to enter a portal through the Force.<ref name="DV24" /> Darth Vader also forged his first red lightsaber at the cave, and [[Snoke]], the First Order Supreme Leader who trained Kylo Ren, wore a [[Snoke's ring|ring]] that featured obsidian carved from the same cave.<ref name="USWNE" />

Corvax Fen was a vaguely hospitable bog that contained irontrees, being one of Mustafar's few such places. Located close to the ruins of Darth Vader's fortress, the fen was guarded by the Alazmec of Winsit, a group of cultists devoted to the Sith Lord.<ref name="Corvax Fen DB">{{Databank|corvax-fen|Corvax Fen}}</ref> Barren and noxious, the marsh was surrounded by a misty air that smelt of [[ozone]]. It contained a shallow lake of brackish water that was covered in an [[oil]]y film.<ref name="TROS EE" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Early conception===
{{Quote|It was a whole part of the plot that essentially got cut out. It may be in one of the sequels. ''[…]'' Ben and Vader have a confrontation, just like they have in ''Star Wars'', and Ben almost kills Vader. As a matter of fact, he falls into a volcanic pit and gets fried and is one destroyed being.|George Lucas on August 25, 1977, the earliest known mention of what would become Mustafar|<ref name="Rolling Stone">{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/george-lucas-the-wizard-of-star-wars-2-232011|text=George Lucas: The Wizard of 'Star Wars'|author=Scanlon, Paul|date=1977-08-25|work=[https://www.rollingstone.com Rolling Stone]|archivedate=20200623204338}}</ref>}}
[[File:RMQ-TheLavaThrone-RotJAVA.png|thumb|left|342px|Concept art of the Emperor's Throne Room situated above a lava lake, by Ralph McQuarrie]]
By [[August 25]], [[1977]], [[George Lucas]] conceptualized Darth Vader's transformation into a cyborg happening after a duel with Ben Kenobi and the father of Luke Skywalker. The father is killed by Vader, who is confronted and nearly killed by Kenobi. Vader falls into a volcanic pit and is severely injured, necessitating his use of cybernetics.<ref name="Rolling Stone" /> The concept of a lava duel was revisited in the earliest versions of ''Return of the Jedi''. In those versions, Luke Skywalker fights Darth Vader over a lava lake in the [[Emperor's Throne Room]], located in a cave in the lowest levels of the Imperial capital [[Had Abbadon]]. Although this was visualized by veteran ''Star Wars'' concept artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]], the concept was not carried over to the final script.<ref name="Making of ROTJ">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> The concept of Kenobi dueling Vader, while altered with Skywalker's father now being Vader himself, was realized in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], twenty-eight years after the original film.<ref name="ROTS" />

===''Revenge of the Sith''===
====Symbolism and naming====
{{Quote|Mufasta's been around for a long time. I've always had this set piece: the end between Obi-Wan and Anakin. I knew that's where this movie was going to end up. It's all this volcanic land, with lava shooting up, so it's almost monochromatic in its red-and-blackness. I've had that image with me for a long time.|George Lucas on Mustafar, known as "Mufasta" at that point in the production of ''Revenge of the Sith''|<ref name="Making of RotS">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>}}
[[File:MustafarHellscape-SWBC52.png|thumb|right|350px|Mustafar was a major setting in ''Revenge of the Sith'']]
Released in [[2005]], ''Revenge of the Sith'' marked the first appearance of Mustafar.<ref name="ROTS" /> Brought up as a major location of the film, the volcano world becomes the culmination of the lava designs from the development of the original trilogy. Whilst the planet is named "Mufasta" in earlier concepts for ''Revenge of the Sith'', the finalized spelling was in place by [[October 25]], [[2002]]; George Lucas had decided to dedicate about twenty to thirty minutes screen time to the planet he respelled, and planned to include a major fight as well as a "love scene" there. Despite the new spelling, draftspeople and model-makers working on the film in [[Wikipedia:Sydney|Sydney]], [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australia]] spelt the planet name as "Mustafa" when labelling an early 3-D rendering of the lava world's Separatist war room.<ref name="Making of RotS" /> "Mustafa," [[Wikipedia:Romanization|romanized]] from the [[Wikipedia:Arabic|Arabic]] (أَلْمُصْطَفَى), is an [[Wikipedia:Names and titles of Muhammad|epithet]] of [[Wikipedia:Muhammad|Muhammad]] in the [[Wikipedia:Quran|Qur'an]] that means "The Chosen."<ref name="Quran">{{WebCite|url=http://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A2002.02.0006%3Asura%3D22%3Averse%3D75|text=The Quran, sura 22, verse 75|archivedate=20200625100706}}</ref>

Writer-director George Lucas intended the lava planet to symbolize the [[Wikipedia:Bible|Biblical]] [[Wikipedia:Hell|hell]].<ref name="Hell">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/star-wars-goes-to-hell|text='Star Wars' Goes To Hell|author=Leung, Rebecca|date=2005-03-10|archivedate=20200527074221}}</ref> The color scheme of the planet's wilderness was emblematic of the anger and regret that fueled the duel between Skywalker and Kenobi, with the fires and lava floes visualizing the characters' feelings and the conflict between them.<ref name="Insider 216">{{InsiderCite|216|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the Star Wars Galaxy|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}}</ref> Lucas also said that Anakin Skywalker's injuries that were inflicted by Mustafar led to the loss of his power in the Force; Darth Sidious' plan for his new apprentice to become more powerful than himself was derailed by Obi-Wan Kenobi.<ref name="GL story">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2005/02/star-wars-george-lucas-story|text=Behind the Scenes of Star Wars: Episode III––Revenge of the Sith, and The Making of George Lucas's Empire|author=Windolf, Jim|date=2014-02-19|archivedate=20200503111642}}</ref>

====Concept art====
Before Lucasfilm artists finished work on the [[2002]] prequel trilogy film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], George Lucas wanted ideas of what his lava planet for Episode III would look like.<ref name="Church tweet1">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1381393884249395202|[[Ryan Church]]|quote=#StarWars - very early Episode 3 concepts for Mustafar, sketched in Corel Painter-|archivedate=20210411234920}}</ref> Prequel trilogy concept artist [[Doug Chiang]] had previous made sketches of Mustafar's volcanoes, as well as a castle on the world.<ref name="ROTS doc" /> The Episode III art department began working in early 2002,<ref name="Art Dep">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/profile/f20030204/index.html|text=Meet the Episode III Art Department}}</ref> and at [[Skywalker Ranch]], artists conceptualized Lucas' lava planet as either a technologically advanced world or a wild, primordial location.<ref name="Featurette">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' (Featurette: Mustafar Overview)</ref>

Concept Design Supervisor [[Ryan Church]] made concepts of both using [[Wikipedia:Corel Painter|Corel Painter]],<ref name="Church tweet1" /> and one such piece<ref name="Featurette" /> featured [[Wikipedia:Gothic architecture|Gothic]] constructs of skyscraper proportions.<ref name="Church tweet2">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1400133722708471813|[[Ryan Church]]|quote=One of the first pieces I ever did for Episode 3- here's the page from my old sketchbook where I work some of it out- we were trying a lot of ideas at this early point, the main question being how technological/natural Mustafar was... Thanks for sharing @kershed !!!|archivedate=20210602172721}}</ref> When Lucas was shown one of Church's more abstract and fanciful concepts for Mustafar, the director said that he wanted a more grounded design.<ref name="Church tweet3">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1331282810888339458|[[Ryan Church]]|archivedate=20201124175017}}</ref>

The concept artists who worked on Mustafar for Episode III include Concept Design Supervisors Ryan Church and [[Erik Tiemens]], [[Aaron McBride]],<ref name="Making of RotS" /> and [[Derek Thompson]],<ref name="Thompson">{{Twitter|kershed|status/1457774291722801162|[[Paul Duncan]]|archivedate=20211108183222}}</ref> amongst others.<ref name="Art Dep" /> McBride originally designed the [[Pau'an]]s seen in the final film as natives of Mustafar, although Lucas decided to use his designs for the residents of [[Utapau]] by 2004.<ref name="McBride tweet">{{Twitter|AmcbToraidhe|status/1219396094175526912|[[Aaron McBride]]|archivedate=20200120230925}}</ref>

After the artists made a variety of concepts, such as controlled mineral-harvesting environments complete with lava dams as well as an orbital ring structure that siphoned energy from the lava world, the two extremes ultimately coalesced into what became of Mustafar: a blend of lava-reliant technology and an untamed hellscape.<ref name="Featurette" /><ref name="Ryan Church">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ryanchurch.com/star-wars-iii|text=STAR WARS III — RYANCHURCH.COM|archivedate=20200711204447}}</ref> With Lucas stating that the film would begin with seven battles on seven planets in June of 2002, Church made his ring world concept as a ''Star Wars'' take on a [[Wikipedia:Dyson sphere|Dyson sphere]].<ref name="Church tweet4">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1400506152908070912|[[Ryan Church]]|archivedate=20210603174555}}</ref> In addition, Church conceptualized a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] crashing on the world as a result of a battle overhead<ref name="Mufasta battle1">{{Twitter|kershed|status/1419357204755398659|[[Paul Duncan]]|archivedate=20210725180205}}</ref>—he had little knowledge of the plot at the time, and thought that the duel between Kenobi and Skywalker could start on the ship and continue after it crashes on the surface of "Mufasta."<ref name="Mufasta battle2">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1701615732495438301|[[Ryan Church]]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/o72na}}</ref> A [[June 17]] piece by Tiemens depicts several Venators attacking the world.<ref name="Mufasta battle3">{{Twitter|kershed|status/1405607748767830024|[[Paul Duncan]]|archivedate=20210617192624}}</ref>

Since Lucas insisted that designs for different worlds be instantly distinguishable, owing to the many new planets introduced in Episode III, Church first made a sketch of a Mustafar chamber without color, dated to [[September 26]], 2002. While the Episode III artists did not know the function of Mustafar beside the apparent ending when it was made, the piece features an imposing "alien-imperial" throne.<ref name="Mufasta chamber">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1442534410700541954|[[Ryan Church]]|archivedate=20210927170022}}</ref> A later piece by Church conveys the magnitude of the world's dangers by showing various technological apparatus keeping a Mustafar bunker together amid lava dams and lavafalls, with a ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer docking at the facility. Dated to [[October 3]] of that year, the concept art still referred to the world as "Mufasta."<ref name="Mufasta bunker view">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1445102270362779654|[[Ryan Church]]|archivedate=20211004202806}}</ref>

====Animatics====
{{Quote|Our director's come up with a really good idea, which I think we'll probably use. I'm not quite sure how we're gonna do this, but what he wants to do ''[…]'' if they get down to the end and it breaks off so that it goes and lands in a river of lava, and they're on it.|George Lucas, relaying Steven Spielberg's ideas for the duel on Mustafar|<ref name="Within a Minute">{{YouTube|video=VgS3pt0yMvs|text=Star Wars Within A Minute: The Making Of Episode III Documentary|channel=mranderson00001|name=mranderson00001}}</ref>}}
George Lucas revised his drafts for the film as the concept art for Mufasta developed, and left details of the duel between Vader and Kenobi untouched for guest director [[Steven Spielberg]] to form ideas for, based on concept art approved by Lucas during his meetings with the art department.<ref name="Making of RotS" /> During an art department meeting, Lucas relayed Spielberg's idea that Vader and Kenobi fight on an extended arm of a Mustafar facility that would break off and fall into the lava flows below. Another idea involves Vader and Kenobi taking shelter behind a ledge as a screen of embers fly down from a spurt of lava, bouncing around and catching on fire. To explain the arm breaking off the Mustafar facility, the art department suggested to Lucas that the film shows lava melting through the structure.<ref name="ROTS doc">[[Star Wars home video releases#Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' DVD (''Within a Minute'')]]</ref> Along with animatics supervisor [[Daniel D. Gregoire]], Spielberg helped pre-visualize the Mustafar duel as well as the the Utapau chase scene, both as a favor to Lucas and to learn the latest pre-visualization methods for his own 2005 science fiction film, [[Wikipedia:War of the Worlds (2005 film)|''War of the Worlds'']].<ref name="YBYNE">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref>

====Supporting scenery====
Having heard news that [[Mount Etna]], a volcano on the island of [[Wikipedia:Sicily|Sicily]] in [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]], was erupting in late October, 2002, George Lucas asked [[Wikipedia:Film producer|film producer]] [[Rick McCallum]] to arrange the filming of the ongoing volcanic eruption for Mustafar's imagery. With approval from the Italian government and a local guide, acclaimed [[Wikipedia:Documentary film|documentary filmmaker]] and [[Wikipedia:Cinematographer|cinematographer]] [[Ron Fricke]]<ref name="Making of RotS" /> accompanied McCallum at the site for over a week,<ref name="ROTS doc" /> capturing the bursting lava on a camera rented from a company in [[Wikipedia:Milan|Milan]].<ref name="Making of RotS" />

[[File:Mustafar_matte.jpg|thumb|right|300px||Brett Northcutt's animated, cycloramic background matte painting of Mustafar.]]
Amongst other images, lava fountain elements shot by Fricke were incorporated by<ref name="Matte">{{ArtStation|username=bnorthcutt|url=artwork/8Q96q|name=Brett Northcutt|text=Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith (2005), Brett Northcutt}}</ref> digital matte artist [[Brett Northcutt]]<ref name="Brett Northcutt ILM">{{ILM|url=people/brett-northcutt|text=Brett Northcutt | Industrial Light & Magic|date=2015-09-18}}</ref> at the Digital Environments department<ref name="ROTS doc" /> into an animated background cyclorama used in ''Revenge of the Sith''.<ref name="Matte" /> A mesh of various assets that also included stills of gravel at the [[Industrial Light & Magic]] parking lot and computer generated images, the matte painting comprised of 25,000 pixels and took several months to make, and served as the backdrop for Mustafar in the film.<ref name="ROTS doc" />

====Photography and editing====
Principal photography began in [[Wikipedia:Fox Studios Australia|Fox Studios]] in Sydney, Australia on [[June 30]], [[2003]].<ref name="Making of RotS" /> On [[July 13]], from Skywalker Ranch, Ryan Church made another Mustafar piece to communicate to various film departments of the layout of the Mustafar duel. The piece gives a general idea of the environment in which it would take place and the direction of the battle.<ref name="Church tweet5">{{Twitter|rchurchdesign|status/1415013286920130561|[[Ryan Church]]|archivedate=20210713182042}}</ref>

''Revenge of the Sith''{{'s}} main model for Mustafar measured eight meters wide and eleven meters long,<ref name="BMF 17" /> and was used for establishing shots of Mustafar's surface surrounding the mining facility.<ref name="ROTS doc" /> Resin and paint were added to the model, which was carved from high density foam and had a clear plastic glazing base. Between the rocky elements, the model revealed three channels of the transparent plastic for the flow of simulated lava—which was made from tens of thousands of liters of [[Wikipedia:Hypromellose|methocel]] with yellow dye. In order to achieve the effect of oozing, glowing lava, ILM employees such as [[Todd Lookinland]] initially poured buckets of methocel into the upper end of the model, which they tipped by ten degrees, and placed studio lights of 250,000 [[Wikipedia:Watt|watts]] beneath the plastic channels that the "lava" through. The thickness of the methocel determined the varying shades of red, orange, and yellow resulting from the creative lighting, and black powdered cork was further sprinkled onto the liquid to simulate rocks being carried by the lava flow. An elaborate pump and filtration was installed to recycle the methocel from the bottom on the model back up to the top, maintaining its steady movement.<ref name="BMF 17" />

ILM further filmed faux explosions using additional methocel on an outdoor lot, as well as the lava bank at the end of Vader and Kenobi's duel—combined with their main lava flow model, Mustafar's model sequences took ILM eight months to film—the longest model shoot in the company's history. The final visuals of the fighting sequence comprise of multiple motion-control shots of the main model, digital animation,<ref name="BMF 17" /> and close up and action shots of Anakin Skywalker actor, [[Hayden Christensen]], and Obi-Wan Kenobi actor, [[Ewan McGregor]]. George Lucas and editor [[Roger Barton]] further incorporated the Mount Etna footage as both their own frames and as elements within other shots of the Mustafar sequences.<ref name="ROTS doc" /> When Vader and Kenobi fight on the fallen mining complex arm, the lavafall<ref name="ROTS" /> flows backwards as a result of an edit by George Lucas to ensure the camera follows the duelists in a single direction as they progress.<ref name="ROTS doc" />

===''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''===
{{Quote|Mustafar was also a big deal for me, 'cause I argued with George about that, I said, 'Really, Mustafar?' Because that's where the whole thing with Vader happens ''[…]'' You find your fan-self clashing with the story that George wants to tell, 'cause we hold everything—'Oh, it's so precious to me, and nobody can know about Mustafar!" ''[…]'' We take it to such this uber-serious level and it always takes George to, you know, snap you out of it sometimes and say, 'But this a great ending to this trilogy ''[of episodes]''.'|Dave Filoni, on his initial reluctance to use Mustafar on the show|<ref name="CotF Featurette">{{SW|url=video/children-of-the-force-episode-featurette|text="Children of the Force" Episode Featurette}}</ref>}}
An earlier version of the story for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' [[The Clone Wars: Season One|Season One]] episode "[[Liberty on Ryloth]]" featured [[Mace Windu]] rescuing [[Twi'lek]] captives from a prison suspended over a volcanic caldera. Although this was cut when production paintings of the setting ended up looking too similar to Mustafar,<ref name="Liberty on Ryloth Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/liberty-on-ryloth-trivia-gallery|text="Liberty on Ryloth" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}}</ref> the location was revived for the [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|Season Four]] episodes "[[Slaves of the Republic]]"<ref name="Slaves of the Republic Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/slaves-of-the-republic-trivia|text="Slaves of the Republic" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 2}}</ref> and "[[Escape from Kadavo]]" as the [[Kadavo slave processing facility]].<ref name="Escape from Kadavo">{{TCW|Escape from Kadavo}}</ref>

[[File:AnakinSeduced-GOM.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The symbolic Well of the Dark Side at the ethereal realm of Mortis.]]
Mustafar itself made an appearance in the show's [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] episode "[[Children of the Force]]," serving as the final destination of a three-part arc in the series.<ref name="Children of the Force" /> Development of the planet for the show was challenging for the ''Clone Wars'' team, as the lava and explosion visuals required for the episode called for significant effects work. Supervising director [[Dave Filoni]] also noted that Mustafar's inclusion in the show was initially difficult for him as a fan; to him, the planet was too important to Anakin's story in ''Revenge of the Sith'' to be included earlier in the timeline.
